correction: Set needsEngineWork:true on every consumable/drug record in the chunk, with the note "requires an active-effect gate (drug stage or elixir duration), not inventory possession". Uniformly, so the flag can be used as the triage filter.

problem: Two issues, both minor. (1) The record reads "While wearing a stole of civility, you receive a +2 item bonus to Diplomacy checks...", but neither skill entry carries the wearing gate, unlike every other worn/held item in the chunk (bullhook-greater, spangled-riders-suit, kortos-diamond, staff-of-the-black-desert all state theirs). (2) The third entry turns the once-per-day activation ("You gain 10 temporary Hit Points, which last for 10 minutes", Requirements: you are a human) into a targetKind:'hp' bonus — that is an activated effect, not a modifier to a displayed stat, and the same chunk excluded the jawbreaker shield's reaction on exactly that reasoning.
correction: Add "while wearing the stole" to both skill conditions. Decide one policy for activated non-modifier effects and apply it to the stole's temp HP and sun-orchid-poultice's 20 temp HP together — either both are registered as hp entries or neither is (jawbreaker-shield's reaction was excluded).

problem: The classification (+4 item to the listed Craft subjects, +1d6 vs orcs) is correct and the engineNote rightly calls out that passiveEffects.skills.crafting = 4 over-applies a subject-restricted bonus to every Crafting check. But it misses a second, identical over-application in the same record: passiveEffects.senses grants "greater darkvision" unconditionally, while the text says "If you are a dwarf, you gain greater darkvision while holding the axe. If you are not a dwarf, you are Stupefied 4 while holding the axe" — so a non-dwarf carrying the axe currently gets free greater darkvision and none of the penalties.
correction: Extend the engineNote to cover the sense: greater darkvision is gated on being a dwarf AND holding the axe, and the non-dwarf/orc penalties (stupefied 4, drained 4, enfeebled 4) are unmodelled. Neither is expressible with the listed target kinds, so this is an engine/data note, not a new bonus entry.

problem: Encoding bug: situational is true but there is NO bonuses array, so the entry is empty. The reading itself is right ('If the animal companion already has scent, IT gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception when using scent against fiends' — the companion, not the PC), but every other other-creature case in this same batch is encoded situational:false + needsEngineWork:true (guiding-shot, shielded-recovery, area-armor, shield-from-arrows, blanket-defense, lesson-of-the-broken-wing). As written this record is inconsistent and would either produce a registry entry with nothing to display or, worse, a star on the PC with no text.
correction: Set situational:false with reasonIfNot 'The +2 circumstance bonus is to the animal companion's Perception, not the character's', and keep needsEngineWork:true + engineNote 'needs a companion-stat situational lane; conditions are doubly narrow (only when the companion uses its scent sense, and only against fiends)'.

problem: The engineNote states as settled fact that the Will-vs-fear increase is 'granted to your allies' and therefore out of reach for this sheet. That is only one reading. The base class feature it modifies (classFeatures/commanders-banner) says the aura 'gives you and all allies in a a +1 status bonus to Will saves and DCs against fear effects' — the commander explicitly DOES receive the base +1. Whether Glorious Banner raises the commander's own bonus to +2 is genuinely ambiguous (the same sentence's next clause switches to 'you and affected allies', which cuts the other way), so it should not be closed off with needsHumanDecision:false. The three marked bonuses (+1 status to AC / Fortitude / Reflex) are correct.
correction: Keep the three AC/Fort/Reflex entries as-is, but set needsHumanDecision:true with the question: 'Commander's Banner gives the +1 status vs fear to "you and all allies"; does Glorious Banner's increase to +2 apply to the commander's own Will saves/DCs vs fear, or literally only to allies?' Also worth recording in the note that the commander's own baseline +1 status to Will saves vs fear lives on classFeatures/commanders-banner, which the feats-only lookup can never reach.

problem: The engineNote's factual claim is false: 'this archetype's own dedication does not necessarily grant it [Warfare Lore]'. war-mage-dedication (this feat's own listed prerequisite) reads 'You also gain the Additional Lore general feat for Warfare Lore. If you were already trained in Warfare Lore, you become trained in a Lore skill of your choice.' — so every character who can take Siege Ritualist is guaranteed to have Warfare Lore. The classification (+2 circumstance, skill lore:warfare, situational) and the lore:warfare key form are both correct.
correction: Replace the engineNote's second sentence with: 'Warfare Lore is always present — War Mage Dedication, the prerequisite, grants the Additional Lore feat for Warfare Lore — so the star will always render once the app models that grant.'

problem: The engineNote's factual claim is false: 'there are two records with this id text in core.json (Player Core and Battlecry! printings) with identical wording'. There is exactly one record keyed guiding-shot, source 'Pathfinder Battlecry!' — no duplicate exists in any collection. The classification (situational:false, ally-only, 'the next creature other than you') is correct.
correction: Drop the duplicate-record sentence from the engineNote; keep only the ally-targeted-buff-lane gap.

problem: The bonus string '+4 circumstance (the shield's Take Cover value) instead of the usual +2' hard-codes a baseline that is only right for a tower shield. In core.json tower-shield has acBonus 2 (description: 'AC increases to +4 if you are using the Take Cover action') but fortress-shield has acBonus 3, and its description gives no number at all ('Getting the higher bonus for this shield requires using the Take Cover action while the shield is raised'). The feat text itself never states any number, so 'the usual +2' is an invented constant for one of the two shields the feat names.
correction: Phrase the magnitude shield-relative, e.g. bonus: 'your raised shield's higher Take Cover AC value (tower shield: +4 instead of +2)' with the engineNote already-correct point that the number must be read off the equipped shield and REPLACES rather than stacks with the raised-shield circumstance bonus.

problem: needsEngineWork is set true on the grounds that "'speed' is not in the current SituationalTarget union". Per the target schema I was given, 'speed' IS a permitted target kind, so this is a false engine-work flag on an otherwise correct entry (the record does say "+10-foot status bonus to speed" at Stage 1). Everything else — value, status type, Stage-1 gating — checks out.
correction: Set needsEngineWork false and drop the union complaint from engineNote (keep the note that quickened / Drained 2 / Stupefied 2 are conditions, not bonuses). Separately, reword the 'when': "(1 round after you Interact to take it)" reads as a 1-round delay; the record has NO Onset line — the 1 round is the duration of Stage 1. Use "while Stage 1 is active (1 round; maximum duration 1 minute)".

problem: Same false engine-work flag: needsEngineWork true because "'speed' is not yet in the SituationalTarget union". 'speed' is a permitted kind in the schema. The bonus data itself is right — the umbrella record does say "You gain an item bonus to Athletics checks and you gain the listed status bonus to your Speed" with +2/+3/+4 and +10/+15/+20 ft in the graded blocks, and item-vs-status types are correctly distinguished.
correction: Set needsEngineWork false; keep only the substantive part of engineNote (umbrella record carries no concrete numbers; the -1 AC / -2 Reflex drawback has no slot in this schema). Also consider whether an umbrella record with a range string as its bonus ("+2 / +3 / +4 item") should be registered at all, since the three graded ids carry the real numbers.

problem: needsEngineWork true solely because of the claimed missing 'speed' kind. Record text confirms "+2 item bonus to Athletics checks" and "+10 foot status bonus to your Speed", Duration 1 minute — the entry is otherwise accurate.
correction: Set needsEngineWork false; retain the note about the one-size-larger rider and the -1 AC / -2 Reflex penalty.

problem: needsEngineWork true solely because of the claimed missing 'speed' kind. Record confirms +3 item Athletics / +15-foot status Speed / 10 minutes.
correction: Set needsEngineWork false.

problem: needsEngineWork true solely because of the claimed missing 'speed' kind. Record confirms +4 item Athletics / +20-foot status Speed / 1 hour.
correction: Set needsEngineWork false.

problem: needsEngineWork true only for the 'speed' union claim. The data is correct and well-judged: the record's Activate entry reads "You gain a +1 item bonus to Stealth checks and a +10-foot item bonus to your Speed for 1 minute", and the spec correctly types this Speed bonus as ITEM (unlike applereed/plasma-hype/snowshoes, which are status) and correctly ties it to the activation rather than to wearing the harness.
correction: Set needsEngineWork false; keep the (important) engineNote that this is activation-gated and must not be folded into totals.

problem: needsEngineWork true only for the 'speed' union claim. Record confirms "+5-foot status bonus to their Speed while moving across snow or ice".
correction: Set needsEngineWork false; keep the note that the difficult-terrain clause is not a bonus.

problem: needsEngineWork true on two grounds, both weak. (a) "'strikeDamage' is not in the current SituationalTarget union" — strikeDamage IS a permitted kind in the schema. (b) "gated on the TARGET being frightened, an enemy state the sheet cannot test" — the whole registry is display-only (the file header says so explicitly: "It is DISPLAY-ONLY: nothing here changes a computed number"), so an untestable condition is normal, not engine work. Both bonuses themselves verify exactly against the text.
correction: Set needsEngineWork false. Keep the Drained-2-if-not-unholy rider as a note. Optionally tighten the 'when' on the Perception leg: the record says "When worn" (the invested trait is on the item, but the text conditions on wearing).

problem: The engineNote asserts as fact that the trained-in-Survival requirement "is attached to the Calculate activity, NOT to the identify-celestial-bodies bonus". The record does not say that — it states it flatly and unqualified: "To use an astrolabe, the holder must be trained in Survival." That sentence precedes the Calculate description and reads as a general gate on using the item. The spec's conclusion (do not bind the bonus to skill 'survival') is still right — being trained in Survival is a prerequisite, not the skill rolled — but the justification is invented and the 'when' string omits a stated requirement.
correction: Drop the "attached to the Calculate activity" claim from engineNote and add the prerequisite to the condition text: "on checks to identify celestial bodies, if you are trained in Survival (astrolabe held in two hands...)". Apply the same fix to astrolabe-standard and astrolabe-mariners, which share the identical sentence. Keep the needsHumanDecision question about which skill key to bind to. Minor: on the umbrella record the 'when' folds in "the standard model works only on steady ground", a restriction that belongs to the standard grade only.

problem: Coverage is inverted across the sovereign-steel family. The material text — "All sovereign steel items (including weapon and armor below) ... grant their bonus to saves the owner makes specifically to protect the item from magic" — explicitly names armor, yet the +4 circumstance save leg is registered ONLY on the two Sovereign Steel Object records (raw material priced per Bulk, which the spec itself doubts should ever star) and NOT on the three armor records, which are the ones a character actually wears. The +1 circumstance AC vs spell attack rolls on the armor records is correct and verified.
correction: Decide one way and apply it consistently across sovereign-steel-armor, sovereign-steel-armor-standard-grade and sovereign-steel-armor-high-grade vs sovereign-steel-object-standard-grade / -high-grade: either add the "+4 circumstance, on a save you make specifically to protect this sovereign steel item from magic (e.g. vs. rusting grasp)" leg to the armor records too, or drop it from the Object records as an unrollable/GM-side effect. Note the armor records' own description text does not repeat the +4 clause (it lives on the material record), so if the rule is strict grounding in the record's own text, the Object entries are the ones to drop.

problem: The condition is narrowed and the engineNote invents a Paizo typo that the text does not support. The record reads: 'you can instead attempt a Lore check with a +2 circumstance bonus if the target is trained in that Lore or could be identified by that Lore when Recalling Knowledge.' That is a DISJUNCTION with two qualifying branches. The spec's `when` keeps only the second branch ('if that Lore could identify it') and silently drops the first. The engineNote then asserts the first branch 'reads as a Paizo typo for "if you are trained in that Lore"' — that is an invented rewrite. The printed clause is coherent as written: Dad Joke is a lovingly tailored joke, so a Lore the TARGET is trained in (Farming Lore for a farmer) is exactly the kind of Lore you would build the pun from. Rewriting a printed condition on a typo hunch is the 'condition invented or broadened beyond what the text says' failure mode.
correction: Restore both printed branches and drop the typo claim. Use when: 'when you use Dad Joke and substitute a Lore check for the skill that would identify the target, if the target is trained in that Lore or that Lore could identify it'. Keep bonus '+2 circumstance', targetKind 'skill'. Keep needsEngineWork true, but restate the engine gap accurately: the registry keys Lore individually as `lore:*` (see the SituationalTarget doc comment in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts), so there is no key meaning 'whichever Lore fits the target'; skill 'lore' is a placeholder for a missing any-Lore target. If the typo reading is still suspected, that belongs in needsHumanDecision as a question, not applied as a silent edit to the condition.

problem: The needsHumanDecision question presents only two readings and omits the most likely one, so the Acrobatics row as written is probably over-broad. Text: '+1 item bonus to unarmed attack rolls, Acrobatics checks, and Reflex saves and DCs to Escape, Grab an Edge, or avoid falling prone.' The spec asks only 'does the qualifier scope the Reflex half, or all three?' — but the natural third reading is that it scopes the Acrobatics AND Reflex halves and leaves only unarmed attacks unqualified, because every action in the trailing list is an Acrobatics/Reflex action (Escape can be an Acrobatics check, Grab an Edge is a Reflex save, avoiding falling prone is Acrobatics or Reflex). Under the spec's chosen reading the sheet stars ALL Acrobatics while the clothing is worn, which is a broader claim than the sentence supports. Second problem: the engineNote suggests the unarmed-attack and Acrobatics halves 'could be treated as flat item bonuses in the maths instead of stars'. Doing that for unarmed attacks would be a real bug — Handwraps of Mighty Blows already supply an ITEM bonus to unarmed attacks, item bonuses do not stack, so folding this into the maths would silently inflate the strike total for any character with handwraps.
correction: Rewrite the question to offer three readings: (a) qualifier scopes only Reflex saves/DCs; (b) qualifier scopes Acrobatics and Reflex, leaving only unarmed attacks unconditional; (c) qualifier scopes all three. Flag (b) as the reading the sentence structure best supports, and until the owner rules, scope the Acrobatics entry with when: 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing, to Escape, Grab an Edge, or avoid falling prone' rather than the bare 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing'. Delete the suggestion to move any part of this into the maths, or replace it with an explicit warning that the unarmed-attack half must stay display-only because it is an item bonus that does not stack with Handwraps of Mighty Blows.

problem: `situational: false` is being used to mean 'out of scope' rather than its defined meaning ('unconditional, so it belongs in the maths'), and the chunk applies it inconsistently. Six records whose bonus lands on someone other than the character (fear-no-pain, swift-support, bounce-boost, personalized-poisoning, guardians-deflection-swashbuckler, snap-out-of-it-marshal) are marked situational TRUE with an empty bonus list, while eight Kingmaker records with the same 'nothing lands on a character stat' shape are marked situational FALSE with an empty list. Worse, several kingdom specs contradict their own flag: aon-fortified-fiefs is false yet its engineNote says 'within that subsystem both modifiers WOULD be situational', and aon-inspiring-entertainment is false yet its engineNote says 'within that subsystem this one is clearly situational'. aon-civil-service is the same case — '+2 status bonus to New Leadership checks' is restricted to one named kingdom activity, so it is conditional, not unconditional. A downstream reader taking `situational: false` at its documented meaning would conclude these are flat bonuses.
correction: Unify the two families on one encoding. Recommended: reserve `situational: false` for genuinely unconditional bonuses, and mark every 'nothing lands on a character statistic' record as situational true + bonuses [] + needsEngineWork true, with the reason (ally-facing / companion-facing / kingdom subsystem) in engineNote. Under that rule, flip aon-civil-service, aon-cooperative-leadership, aon-crush-dissent, aon-fortified-fiefs, aon-free-and-fair, aon-insider-trading and aon-inspiring-entertainment to situational true with empty bonuses. aon-practical-magic is the one kingdom record that should stay false, because '+1 status bonus to Magic checks' really is unconditional inside its own subsystem. Either way, remove the engineNote sentences that assert the opposite of the flag on the same record.

problem: The engineNote contradicts the data it ships. It says 'the sheet must not present them as bonuses' while the two -1 circumstance penalties are placed in the `bonuses` array, which is exactly what the sheet renders as bonuses. An applier following the note would strip the penalties (losing information the player needs — Harsh Judgment penalises Seeking and Demoralizing everyone except the condemned foe) or render them under a bonus heading, the thing the note forbids. The classification itself is right: the record does read '+2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to Seek your condemned foe and on Intimidation checks to Demoralize them. You have a -1 circumstance penalty to Perception checks to Seek creatures other than your condemned foe...'. The live registry already carries penalty rows in the same array (barbarian-dedication: bonus "-1 (penalty)"; diverse-mystery: bonus "-1 status"), so there is precedent — the note is simply wrong about the convention.
correction: Keep all four rows and delete the contradictory sentence. Follow the existing labeling convention in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts so the display reads as a penalty rather than a bonus — e.g. bonus '-1 circumstance (penalty)' for the two Seek/Demoralize-others rows, matching barbarian-dedication's '-1 (penalty)'. Apply the identical change to the duplicate record aon-harsh-judgment, whose engineNote carries the same contradictory sentence.

problem: CONDITION NARROWED beyond the text. The record says: "Your first attack that hits a frightened creature after you roar and before the end of your next turn gains a +4 circumstance bonus to damage." It says A FRIGHTENED CREATURE — any frightened creature. The spec's `when` restricts it to "a creature frightened by your Dragon Roar", which is an invented narrowing. A player reading the app's condition would wrongly forgo the +4 against a foe frightened by an ally's Demoralize, by Dread Marshal Stance, by a spell, or by an earlier roar's lingering frightened value.
correction: Keep situational:true, targetKind strikeDamage, +4 circumstance. Rewrite the condition to: "on the first attack that hits a frightened creature (any source of frightened) after you Roar, before the end of your next turn; requires Dragon Stance, and the effect ends immediately if you leave Dragon Stance". The stance-exit clause ("Its effects end immediately if you leave Dragon Stance") is also missing from the spec and is worth keeping in the player-facing text.

problem: CLASSIFICATION IS RIGHT, needsEngineWork IS WRONG. The record text is confirmed unconditional ("In addition, you gain a +2 status bonus to Fortitude and Will saving throws." — no trigger, requirement or duration), so situational:false is correct. But the spec asserts it "belongs in the computed save totals" without checking whether it is there. It is not: the core.json record has keys id,name,level,category,traits,rarity,description,source,prerequisites,actionCost,edition and NO `saves` field; a scan shows ZERO feats in core.json carry a `saves` field at all; and grepping C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src for 'peerless-form' returns no matches. The +2 status to Fortitude and Will is currently applied nowhere in the app. Excluding it from this registry as written leaves it silently missing — the exact mirror of the monk-moves defect the same engineer correctly caught.
correction: Keep situational:false, but set needsEngineWork:true with the note: "No feat record in core.json carries a `saves` field and nothing in src references peerless-form, so this unconditional +2 status to Fortitude and Will is not applied by the engine. Either add a feat-level `saves` lane (mirroring the existing `speeds` lane) and backfill peerless-form, or the bonus is lost entirely."

problem: The classification (situational:false, bonus lands on an ALLY's AC) is CORRECT and confirmed by the text. The engineNote's factual claims about the duplicates are WRONG on both counts. It says 'guardians-deflection' is "raw AoN-style text, no level field" — that record DOES have level 4 and category 'class'. It says 'guardians-deflection-swashbuckler' is the "level 4, tidied text" one — true, but that record is marked edition:"superseded", i.e. it is the one already suppressed, not the survivor. The note also misses a THIRD record entirely: 'guardians-deflection-fighter' (Fighter, level 6, edition remaster), a distinct live feat with the same ally-AC-only behaviour.
correction: Keep situational:false and needsEngineWork:true (no target kind for another creature's AC). Replace the note with: "Three records exist: 'guardians-deflection' (swashbuckler, level 4, remaster, raw-text formatting) and 'guardians-deflection-fighter' (fighter, level 6, remaster) are both LIVE and both grant the +2 circumstance only to the ally's AC; 'guardians-deflection-swashbuckler' (level 4) is already edition:'superseded'. Any decision must cover the two live ids."

problem: The classification (situational:false, the +1 circumstance is on the ALLY's Will save) is CORRECT and confirmed. The engineNote's duplicate claim is WRONG in the same way as guardians-deflection: 'snap-out-of-it' DOES have a level field (4), and the "tidied" record is 'snap-out-of-it-marshal', which is already edition:"superseded". More importantly, the note's instruction that "a decision here should cover both" is dangerous because there is a THIRD id, 'snap-out-of-it-pathfinder-agent' (level 8, Pathfinder Agent archetype), which is a DIFFERENT feat — a Medicine check that reduces the value of fascinated/frightened/stunned/stupefied. It grants no typed bonus at all and must not inherit this classification.
correction: Keep situational:false and needsEngineWork:true. Replace the note with: "'snap-out-of-it' (level 4, remaster) is the live record; 'snap-out-of-it-marshal' is already edition:'superseded'. 'snap-out-of-it-pathfinder-agent' is an unrelated feat (Medicine check that reduces a condition's value) with no typed bonus — exclude it, do not apply this decision to it."

problem: Fabricated bonus magnitudes. All eight skill entries state the cognitive mutagen's item bonus is "+2 lesser / +3 moderate / +4 greater / +5 major". core.json's own cognitive mutagen records say otherwise: cognitive-mutagen-lesser "You gain a +1 item bonus", cognitive-mutagen-moderate "+2 item bonus", cognitive-mutagen-greater "+3 item bonus", cognitive-mutagen-major "+4 item bonus". Every grade is overstated by 1, and the +5 grade does not exist at all. The feat text itself ('You also gain the mutagen's item bonus to Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, Medicine, Nature, Performance, Religion, and Survival checks') never names a number, so the figures were invented rather than read.
correction: Replace the bonus string on all 8 entries with: "item bonus equal to the cognitive mutagen's (+1 lesser / +2 moderate / +3 greater / +4 major)". Everything else in this spec is correct and verified: situational true; the skill list (deception, diplomacy, intimidation, medicine, nature, performance, religion, survival) matches the text exactly; the type is item; needsEngineWork true is right because the magnitude is inherited from whichever grade is active; and the Silvertongue clause (penalty suppression) and Serene clause (detection immunity) are correctly excluded.

problem: The spec records an entry on this character's own AC with bonus "-1 circumstance (effective; enemies get +1 to hit you)". The record grants this character no bonus and no penalty. Verified text: "On a success, the targets focus on you and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to hit you, but they're off-guard to all creatures other than yourself." That is a bonus on the ENEMIES' attack rolls — the same category the very same pass correctly flagged needsEngineWork for exigent-aura ("the +4 is a bonus on the ENEMY's saving throw"). Converting it to an AC penalty is also mechanically wrong, not just cosmetically: a circumstance bonus in the attacker's pool competes with THEIR circumstance modifiers (flanking, etc.), whereas a circumstance penalty on your AC competes with YOURS (cover, Raise a Shield). The two produce different numbers whenever either side already has a circumstance modifier. The engineNote's cited precedent is not analogous either — barbarian Rage is written as a penalty to the raging character's own AC; Primadonna is not.
correction: situational: true, needsEngineWork: true, bonuses: [] (remove the ac entry). engineNote: "Enemies within 30 feet who see or hear you and fail against your Performance check gain a +1 circumstance bonus to attack rolls against you for 1 round (3 rounds on a critical success); they are off-guard to everyone else. The only numeric modifier is on the ENEMY's attack roll, so there is nothing to mark on this character's own stats — needs an enemy-side modifier channel, same as exigent-aura. Do not re-express it as a -1 circumstance penalty to AC: that lands in the wrong stacking pool."

problem: The second bonus entry maps "+2 circumstance bonus to your Reflex DC to avoid being Disarmed and Tripped" (verified verbatim) onto targetKind 'save', save 'reflex', and needsEngineWork is NOT set. A Reflex DC is the number an opponent rolls against; it is not a Reflex saving throw this character rolls. As written the entry paints a star on the player's Reflex SAVE row for a bonus that never applies to any save they make. The spec's own engineNote concedes "A DC-side channel would be more correct" but the flag that records exactly that gap was left off, so the wrong entry would ship. (The first entry, +1 circumstance to Athletics to Disarm/Swim/Trip, is verified correct and should stay.)
correction: Keep only the athletics entry: {bonus: '+1 circumstance', when: 'while in Reflective Ripple Stance (unarmored), on Athletics checks to Disarm, Swim, or Trip', targetKind: 'skill', skill: 'athletics'}. Drop the save/reflex entry and set needsEngineWork: true with engineNote: "The stance also gives +2 circumstance to your Reflex DC against attempts to Disarm or Trip you. That is a defence DC others roll against, and no target kind in the list represents a DC — it must not be recorded on save/reflex. Needs a defence-DC channel."

problem: The single perception entry merges two different things into one 'when' string: (a) "Perception checks made to Sense Motive against other elves" and (b) "your Perception DC against Lies spoken by agents of Tanglebriar". I confirmed Political Acumen's text in core.json reads exactly that way, so the inherited condition is right — but (b) is a DC opponents roll against, not a Perception check this character rolls, and needsEngineWork is not set. Same defect as reflective-ripple-stance: half the entry is a stat the app has no representation for, silently folded into a target kind that does exist.
correction: Split into one representable entry plus a flag. Entry: {bonus: '+4 circumstance (replaces Political Acumen's +2)', when: 'on Perception checks to Sense Motive against other elves', targetKind: 'perception'}. Then needsEngineWork: true, engineNote: "Political Acumen's other half — +2 (raised to +4 by this feat) to your Perception DC against Lies spoken by agents of Tanglebriar — is a DC others roll against and has no target kind; needs a defence-DC channel. Also, when both feats are held Political Acumen's +2 must be suppressed rather than stacked."

problem: needsHumanDecision is set asking whether the character can be one of their own Bloc Tactics targets, but the record's own first sentence answers it: "You have experience in undertaking direct action and know how to protect the identity and health of you and your allies when doing so." The feat is explicitly framed as protecting you as well as your allies, so the character is among the selectable targets and both bonuses do reach this sheet. The two bonus entries and their sizes/types are otherwise verified correct against the text ("+4 status bonus to Deception checks to prevent others from seeing through their disguises, and lets them add their level even if untrained" and "a +3 status bonus to saving throws against them" for smoke/fumes/inhaled substances).
correction: Drop needsHumanDecision and the question; raise confidence to high. Keep both bonuses as specified, and cite the opening line as the evidence for self-inclusion: "know how to protect the identity and health of you and your allies". No needsEngineWork required.

problem: The classification (needsEngineWork for a counteract check) is correct and verified, but the engineNote asserts a fact not present in the record: "the counteract modifier here is your Occultism/Religion-style modifier chosen at use time". The record's actual text has the skill names missing entirely — it reads "you use either your or modifier as your counteract modifier" (two literal blanks where the importer dropped the skill links). Naming Occultism/Religion is a guess layered on top of a data defect rather than something grounded in the record.
correction: Keep situational: true and needsEngineWork: true. Rewrite the engineNote to: "The +1 circumstance bonus applies to a COUNTERACT CHECK, which is not one of the available target kinds — needs a counteract-check channel. Note the record's description is also damaged: it reads 'you use either your or modifier as your counteract modifier', with the two skill names stripped by the importer, so the counteract modifier cannot be resolved from this data at all." Worth surfacing separately as a core.json text defect.

problem: needsEngineWork is set to false, but the spec targets 'strikeDamage', which is not a member of SituationalTarget.kind in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts ('skill' | 'save' | 'perception' | 'ac' | 'attack'). The entry cannot be stored or displayed as specified. The text and bonus reading itself is correct: "You gain a circumstance bonus to damage for the Strike equal to twice the number of weapon damage dice."
correction: Set needsEngineWork: true — the registry needs a strikeDamage (or generic damage) target kind before this can be shown; the variable size (2x weapon damage dice) is a second, separate engine need already noted.

problem: Two issues. (1) needsEngineWork:false is wrong for the same reason as pivot-strike — 'strikeDamage' is not a supported target kind. (2) The `when` reads "if it hits the target you just Demoralized", which implies the Demoralize must have succeeded. The record says only "Attempt an Intimidation check to Demoralize, then make one gorilla slam Strike against the same target. If your Strike hits, you gain a circumstance bonus to the damage roll equal to triple the value of the target's frightened condition." The bonus is keyed to the target's frightened value from any source, regardless of whether the Demoralize landed.
correction: Set needsEngineWork: true. Reword `when` to "on the gorilla slam Strike from Gorilla Pound, if it hits — bonus is 3x the target's current frightened value (requires Gorilla Stance)", dropping the implication that the Demoralize must succeed.

problem: needsEngineWork:false is wrong: the first bonus targets 'strikeDamage', which SituationalTarget.kind does not support. (The three-way split of the text and the +1 circumstance readings are correct — the record confirms "the qualifying conditions are clumsy, drained, enfeebled, frightened, sickened, and stupefied" and "+1 circumstance bonus to skill checks to Tumble Through and to perform your style's panache-granting actions until the end of your turn".)
correction: Set needsEngineWork: true, citing the missing strikeDamage target kind and the variable bonus size (count of qualifying conditions).

problem: needsEngineWork:false is wrong: the sole bonus targets 'strikeDamage', which is not in SituationalTarget.kind. The engineNote even argues 'no engine work is strictly needed for display', which is false given the current type. Text reading is otherwise correct.
correction: Set needsEngineWork: true — the registry cannot express a damage target today.

problem: Two issues. (1) needsEngineWork:false is wrong: 'strikeAttack' is not a supported target kind. (2) The record says "a +1 circumstance bonus to your next attack roll or saving throw against that creature" — 'attack roll' covers spell attack rolls and thrown/ranged attacks, not only Strikes, so 'strikeAttack' under-reports.
correction: Set needsEngineWork: true, and target the registry's existing generic 'attack' kind (SituationalTarget.kind includes 'attack') rather than 'strikeAttack'. Keep the exclusive-choice wording in `when`.

problem: The first bonus is recorded as 'strikeAttack', but the record says "a +1 status bonus to their attack rolls" — all attack rolls, not only Strikes. (The ally-only limitation, the +1 status type and the 1 additional spirit damage are all correctly read; needsEngineWork is already true.)
correction: Use the generic 'attack' target kind rather than 'strikeAttack' so spell and ranged attacks are covered. The damage half remains blocked on a missing damage target kind.

problem: The `when` text ("for 1 minute after this reaction fires — once per day, when you critically fail a save against a foe's spell of your chosen tradition") describes only the TRIGGER, not the scope of the upgraded bonus. I checked the referenced feat: spellmasters-resilience reads "You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against spells and effects with that tradition's trait". So the upgraded +2 still applies only against that one tradition. As written a player would add +2 to every save for the minute — a broadened condition.
correction: Reword `when` to something like "for 1 minute, against spells and effects with your chosen tradition's trait (upgraded from Spellmaster's Resilience's +1); triggered once per day when you critically fail such a save — you fail instead".

problem: The `when` asserts "(first success per creature)". The record says only "The first time you successfully Recall Knowledge to identify a creature, ... you gain a +2 circumstance bonus on your next save against an innate spell cast by that creature." Whether 'the first time' means once per creature or once ever is not stated. The spec resolved the ambiguity silently and set needsHumanDecision:false.
correction: Either drop the parenthetical and use the record's own wording ("the first time you successfully Recall Knowledge to identify that creature"), or keep the per-creature reading and set needsHumanDecision: true with the question 'Is Innate Magic Intuition once per creature or once ever?'

problem: The engineNote's supporting claim is false. It says "the registry's `bonus` field already carries effect phrases elsewhere (see situationalBonuses.ts line 76 breath-control)". Line 76 actually reads: bonus: "+1 circumstance", when: "against inhaled threats (success becomes critical success)" — the degree-of-success phrase lives in `when`, not `bonus`. Consequently the Balance entry, which puts "success becomes a critical success" in `bonus`, does not match the registry's actual convention. The two bonuses themselves are correctly read from the record.
correction: Keep the Athletics entry as-is. For the Balance clause, follow line 76: put the effect phrase in `when` (e.g. when: "on Acrobatics checks to Balance while wielding your staff (a success becomes a critical success)") and leave `bonus` empty or as the effect label, and drop the incorrect line-76 citation.

problem: Same field-placement issue: `bonus` is given as "+2 circumstance (a success on the Climb check becomes a critical success)", mixing a numeric modifier and a degree-of-success effect in one field. The registry's convention (situationalBonuses.ts line 76) keeps `bonus` as the bare modifier and puts the effect phrase in `when`. The record text, target (athletics), size and type are all correct, and the claim about content.stances['gorilla-stance'] carrying only a prose `note` plus `strikes` is verified true.
correction: Split the fields: bonus: "+2 circumstance", when: "on Athletics checks to Climb while in Gorilla Stance (a success becomes a critical success)".

problem: WRONG TARGET. The spec maps the clause "Your spells and alchemical items that deal fire damage gain a status bonus to damage equal to half the spell's rank" to targetKind 'spell'. In this app 'spell' is not a generic spellcasting marker — src/rules/explain.ts defines it as `{ kind: 'spell'; entryId: string; which: 'dc' | 'attack' }` and resolves it to 'spell-dc' or 'spell-attack' (explain.ts lines 52 and 133). So this entry would put a star on the spell attack roll / spell DC advertising a bonus that never applies to either of them. It is exactly the mis-target the review was asked to catch: a damage bonus recorded against a roll stat. Note the same spec correctly refuses to use 'hp' for healing output on magic-hands for precisely this reason, so the treatment here is also internally inconsistent.
correction: Drop the 'spell'-targeted entry and return NO bonuses for burn-it, keeping situational:true and needsEngineWork:true. All three sub-bonuses are then unrepresentable for the same reason — there is no spell-damage, item-damage or persistent-damage target kind in the StatRef union (skill/save/perception/ac/classDc/spell/ability/hp/speed/strikeAttack/strikeDamage). Restate the engineNote as: "Grants three damage bonuses — (a) status bonus to fire damage from your spells equal to half the spell's rank, (b) status bonus to fire damage from your alchemical items equal to one-quarter the item's level, minimum +1 for both, and (c) +1 status to persistent fire damage you deal. None map to a target kind: 'spell' is the spell DC/attack roll, not spell damage. Needs a spell-damage / persistent-damage target before this feat can be marked." If the owner would rather show it somewhere than nowhere, that is a needsHumanDecision, not a silent re-use of 'spell'.

problem: MISSING needsEngineWork FLAG. The bonus itself is right (+4 circumstance on checks to Aid, skill 'all', matching the text "You gain a +4 circumstance bonus on checks to Aid"), but the spec's own engineNote states "The attack-roll form of Aid is not covered by a 'skill' target" while needsEngineWork is left unset. Aid RAW is "attempt a skill check or attack roll", so part of this feat's bonus genuinely has no representation. The identical gap on musetouched (Escape via unarmed attack modifier) IS flagged needsEngineWork:true, so the two records are inconsistent and the Aid-via-attack-roll gap would be silently dropped from whatever engine backlog is built from these flags.
correction: Set needsEngineWork: true on cooperative-nature, keeping the existing single bonus entry (+4 circumstance / skill 'all' / "on any check to Aid an ally") unchanged. Keep the engineNote wording, which already names the gap correctly: the attack-roll form of Aid has no target kind, since 'strikeAttack' is per-Strike-instance and would wrongly flag ordinary attacks.

problem: Marked situational:false with the claim "Big Debut grants no bonus of any type to any of your statistics." That is false — the spec's evidence quote stops halfway through the description. The full text ends: "As your first action on your first turn, you can Interact to draw or stow an item of light Bulk as a free action; if this item is a small garment or accessory, such as a fan, a pair of gloves, or a wine glass, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus on Charisma-based skill checks until the end of your turn." This is a real, conditional, typed bonus that would never get a star under the submitted spec.
correction: situational: true. One bonus: bonus "+1 circumstance", when "until the end of your turn, if you spent your first action of your first turn Interacting to draw or stow a small garment or accessory (a fan, gloves, a wine glass) after Big Debut", targets = the four Charisma-based skills: {kind:'skill', detail:'deception'}, {kind:'skill', detail:'diplomacy'}, {kind:'skill', detail:'intimidation'}, {kind:'skill', detail:'performance'}. (Enumerate the four rather than using detail:'all' — the text says "Charisma-based skill checks", not all skills.) The rest of the spec's reasoning stands: the initiative change and the enemy save vs your class/spell DC are correctly not bonuses, and needsEngineWork can stay false for the starred part.

problem: The second emitted bonus puts a SPELL DAMAGE bonus on targetKind 'spell'. In the allowed target list 'spell' is the spellcasting attack/DC stat (there is a separate 'strikeAttack' and 'strikeDamage', but no spell-damage kind). Starring the spell stat with '+status equal to the spell's rank' would read to a player as if their spell attack rolls and spell DC gained up to +10, which is a far larger and completely different claim than the text makes. The record says only: 'Spells you cast from spell slots gain a status bonus to damage against these creatures equal to the rank of the spell; this bonus applies only to spells that deal damage and don't have a duration.' The author already recognised the mismatch in engineNote but emitted the entry anyway — and inconsistently, since the identical class of problem was correctly left unemitted in stalwart-standard and thats-not-natural.
correction: Keep the strikeDamage entry ('+status equal to your number of weapon damage dice', for 3 rounds, against undead / creatures holding an imprisoned soul / creatures you have witnessed create or command undead) and DROP the targetKind:'spell' entry. Leave situational true and needsEngineWork true, with the engineNote asking for a spell-damage marker (a Spells-tab marker or a new kind) plus the unexpressible 'if your spiral is glowing you can redirect the whole package to a willing creature in its light' clause.

problem: The emitted bonus stars skill/deception for a +4 that does not apply to Deception checks at all. The record says: 'you gain a +4 circumstance bonus to your Deception DC to prevent others from seeing through your disguise' — that is the DC observers roll Perception against, not your check modifier. A star on the Deception row is the wrong side of the roll, and the disclaimer buried in the 'when' string does not undo the marker appearing on a stat that gets no bonus. The same author correctly emitted nothing for the Fortitude/Reflex DC half of stalwart-standard and nothing for the Perception DC half of thats-not-natural, so this entry is also internally inconsistent. (Foundry's bodysnatcher.json carries no rule elements, so nothing supports a check-side bonus.)
correction: Emit NO bonuses. Keep situational true and needsEngineWork true with an engineNote saying the +4 circumstance bonus applies to the holder's Deception DC against attempts to see through a Bodysnatcher disguise (and that the transformation auto-defeats Perception DCs to identify the ancestry/creature type), and that the sheet has no skill-DC concept to attach it to. Re-emit as skill/deception only if the app owner later decides a skill-DC marker should live on the skill row.

problem: The single emitted bonus starts at '+3 item' and its 'when' covers only 'improved or greater Lastwall soup'. But the feat's first effect is 'Add Lastwall soup to your list of herbal items', and items/lastwall-soup grants '+2 item bonus to Stealth checks and DCs against undead' — so from feat level 4 through 9 the only soup the feat unlocks gives +2, not +3. The +3 does not exist until 10th level and the +4 until 18th. As written the entry would show a level-4 character a bonus one point too large.
correction: If the app owner answers question (a) with 'register it on the feat', the entry should read: bonus '+2 item (+3 with Lastwall Soup (Improved) at 10th level, +4 with Lastwall Soup (Greater) at 18th level, per the feat text)', when 'for 1 hour after you eat Lastwall soup, to Stealth checks and DCs against undead'. Keep needsHumanDecision true — and note that the +3/+4 conflict in question (b) is real and resolvable: items/lastwall-soup-greater's description is a verbatim copy of the Improved one (it still says 'after consuming a bowl of improved Lastwall soup' and '+3 item bonus' while carrying the greater item's level 18 and 10 temp HP), so the item record looks like the copy-paste bug and the feat's +4 is the likely authority. Add that observation to the question rather than leaving it a coin flip.

problem: The third bonus is filed with targetKind "strikeAttack" but the record's text makes it a SKILL bonus: "you gain a +2 circumstance bonus from Deft Cooperation (instead of a +1 bonus) the first time you attempt an attack roll or attempt a skill check where the bonus would apply." The author flagged this himself in his own question and then shipped it anyway, so the registry would end up with two identical strikeAttack entries and no skill marker at all — the exact 'wrong target' failure mode. (Verified: attack + skill are the two branches; there is no second attack branch.)
correction: Re-target entry 3 to { kind: 'skill', detail: 'all' } (file shape) / targetKind 'skill', skill 'all'. Entries 1 (save/reflex, Reflex DC vs Disarm) and 2 (strikeAttack) are confirmed correct. Note the registry shape actually in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts is { targets: SituationalTarget[], when, bonus } with kind ∈ skill|save|perception|ac|attack and a `detail` field — one record CAN carry several targets in one entry, so the author's stated reason for reusing strikeAttack ('a single record's entries share no way to say skill: all alongside') is factually wrong.

problem: situational:false is a mis-classification. The record says "**Requirements** You are unarmored ... While in Rain of Embers Stance, you gain a +1 status bonus to AC and fire resistance equal to half your level" — that is unambiguously conditional. The author used the `situational` flag to mean 'the app already models it' rather than 'the bonus is unconditional'. Any consumer that reads situational:false as the prompt defines it ('an unconditional bonus belongs in the maths') would fold a permanent +1 status AC into every Rain of Embers character. The engineering conclusion is right (I confirmed content.stances['rain-of-embers-stance'] carries acBonus:{value:1,type:'status'}, applied at src/rules/derive.ts:439 and shown in the breakdown at src/rules/explain.ts:434-435), but it is the wrong field to express it in.
correction: Set situational:true (bonus: '+1 status', when: 'while in Rain of Embers Stance', target ac) and record the exclusion separately — e.g. alreadyModelled:true / excludeFromRegistry:true with the reason 'applied by the stance toggle; starring it would double-count'. Keep the author's policy question, it is the right one to ask. Also worth carrying forward: the stance data does NOT enforce the 'You are unarmored' requirement or the fire resistance, so an armored character can currently toggle the stance and keep the +1.

problem: Condition broadened beyond the text. The record reads: "You hide your identity behind a mask representing an animal of your choice ... You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to saves against divination effects, though sometimes refusing to remove your mask can cause issues in areas that don't respect or understand the magic warrior tradition." problem: The situational:false verdict is right but the reasonIfNot misstates the rule. It claims the potency inheritance is 'the normal rule rather than an extra situational modifier'. problem: Two accuracy issues in an otherwise verbatim-correct spec. problem: Marked situational:false with reasonIfNot "the feat merely extends that already-earned bonus to the second target". That mischaracterises the sweep trait. core.json's text is: "If you're using a weapon that has the sweep trait, its circumstance bonus applies against both targets." Sweep only gives its +1 circumstance bonus "against a target you already attempted to attack this turn"; a Spell Swipe rolls separate Strikes against TWO different creatures, so neither Strike would normally qualify. The feat therefore creates a bonus that would not otherwise exist — it is not an already-earned bonus being carried over. Classifying it as "nothing to star" drops a real conditional bonus (the exact under-coverage the lane exists to fix).
correction: situational: true, one entry — targetKind 'strikeAttack', bonus "+1 circumstance (your weapon's sweep bonus)", when "on both Strikes of a Spell Swipe when you're wielding a sweep weapon". needsEngineWork false; needsHumanDecision optional if the owner wants weapon-trait-derived bonus sizes resolved from the equipped weapon rather than printed as +1. Medium confidence: the deciding text is the sweep trait's own wording, which lives outside this record, so it is worth a second look by the app owner.

problem: situational:true with an empty bonuses array and no reasonIfNot — internally contradictory and schema-invalid. The spec's own engineNote says "Nothing here should light up a star on the player's sheet as written", which is the definition of situational:false. Record text confirms the only typed bonus goes to the enemy: "The target of your Strike gains a +4 circumstance bonus to their Perception DC for this check." No bonus to any stat the character rolls, so no registry entry." Drop the bonuses key; needsEngineWork can stay true only as a note that another creature's DC has no representable target.

problem: needsEngineWork:true is a false alarm, and the spec contradicts itself: the engineNote says starring the Stealth and Perception rows "would imply the character's own rolls improve, which they do not", yet it lists exactly those two targets anyway. correction: Keep both entries (record text verified: "+4 circumstance bonus to the DCs of checks for others to Seek or Steal objects stored inside your arm"; Seek is opposed by your Stealth DC, Steal by your Perception DC). Set needsEngineWork: false and delete the self-contradicting engineNote, replacing it with the covet-hoard precedent. Keep the DC wording inside `when` so the row reads as a DC, not a check bonus.

problem: needsEngineWork:true on the same false premise ("the app has no Perception-DC stat"). problem: The `evidence` is not the record's text. core.json actually reads "...its target takes 1d6. Your eidolon gains an item bonus to this bleed damage equal to the unarmed attack's item bonus to attack rolls. Fix the evidence to the literal text and raise a separate data bug: bloodletting-claws' description lost its "persistent bleed" damage type in core.json.

problem: Marked situational:true but ships NO bonuses array — the spec text says "deliberately no bonuses entry". That is internally contradictory and inconsistent with every other "someone else gets the bonus" case in the same batch (guiding-shot, shielded-recovery, area-armor, shield-from-arrows, blanket-defense, lesson-of-the-broken-wing), all of which were correctly set situational:false. Written as-is it produces a registry key with an empty array, i.e. a star on the character sheet with nothing behind it (or a crash), and the record is keyed by FEAT id so the star would land on the PC.
correction: The reading of the text is right — core.json confirms "If the animal companion already has scent, it gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception when using scent against fiends", and that is the COMPANION's Perception. problem: The classification is right but the engineNote is factually wrong: it claims "there are two records with this id text in core.json (Player Core and Battlecry! printings) with identical wording". core.json contains exactly ONE record with id "guiding-shot" (verified: a single match for the literal `"id":"guiding-shot"`, and a single occurrence of the sentence "Your ranged attack helps guide your allies into striking your enemy's weak point"). Acting on the note would send an implementer hunting for a duplicate key that does not exist.

Replace the duplicate-id sentence with: "The fighter feat `assisting-shot` shares this wording and is likewise ally-only (situational:false) — it needs the same ally-targeted buff lane."

problem: The engineNote's justification for encoding save 'will' is wrong on the facts. It cites "the existing file already puts control-resistance on will (see 'alghollthu-bound', 'ancestral-suspicion')", but situationalBonuses.ts:55 reads: "ancestral-suspicion": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'save', detail: 'all' }, { kind: 'perception' }], when: "against effects that would make you controlled (e.g. Dominate)", bonus: "+2 circumstance" }] — that is save 'all', not will. So the file's closest analogue (same trigger wording: effects that make you controlled) uses 'all', and the cited precedent actually argues against the spec's own choice.
correction: Feat text confirmed verbatim: "you can attempt another saving throw against the effect that caused you to be confused or controlled with a +4 circumstance bonus to the save" — the save type is inherited from the originating effect and is never named. Change the entry to save 'all' (targets: [{ kind: 'save', detail: 'all' }]), matching ancestral-suspicion, with when: "on the extra save Never! grants each time you would attack an ally while confused or controlled". Keep needsHumanDecision:true and the question as written, but fix the cited precedent: only 'alghollthu-bound' (line 48) uses will, and it does so because its own text names a specific effect category; 'ancestral-suspicion' (line 55) uses 'all'.

problem: Under-reports the benefit and closes the question it should have left open. The feat text is confirmed — "You continually benefit from Take Cover without needing to spend an action, as long as you have a shield raised and it's a tower shield, fortress shield, or other shield that grants a higher circumstance bonus to AC when you Take Cover behind it" — but the spec records AC only, with needsHumanDecision:false. core.json's own `take-cover` action record says the benefit is not AC-only: "If you would have standard cover, you instead gain greater cover, which provides a +4 circumstance bonus to AC; to Reflex saves against area effects; and to Stealth checks to hide, sneak, or otherwise avoid detection. Otherwise, you gain standard cover (a +2 circumstance bonus instead)." A permanently-on Take Cover therefore plausibly also boosts Reflex-vs-area and Stealth, and neither is mentioned.
correction: Keep situational:true and the AC entry, but set needsHumanDecision:true with the question: "Great Shield Mastery grants continual Take Cover. core.json's Take Cover record gives a circumstance bonus to AC, to Reflex saves against area effects, and to Stealth to Hide/Sneak, whereas the Tower Shield item record only says 'AC increases to +4 if you are using the Take Cover action'. Does a raised tower/fortress shield confer the full cover package (add save/reflex and skill/stealth entries) or only the shield's AC increase?" Also correct the bonus string's provenance: the '+4' is read off the tower-shield item, and the '+2' it is contrasted with is the standard-cover value from the Take Cover record — not, as the note implies, purely the raised-shield bonus; the magnitude still has to come from the equipped shield, which the fixed-string shape cannot express.

problem: The reading of the text is right (+2 circumstance on the lick/taste Investigate or Recall Knowledge check; the automatic poison check is a GM secret roll with no bonus), but the spec misses a collision: FEAT_SITUATIONAL already contains a "supertaster" key at src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:321 — `[{ targets: [{ kind: 'perception' }], when: "Perception to detect alterations/additives in food or drink you consume", bonus: "+2 circumstance" }]`. Delete line 321's perception entry and author only `"supertaster": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'skill', detail: 'all' }], when: "when you lick or taste something while Investigating or Recalling Knowledge to identify it, and the taste is relevant (GM's call)", bonus: "+2 circumstance" }]`. Flag the deleted perception entry to the app owner as a pre-existing data bug in the registry.

problem: The classification is correct but the record is already in the registry, and identically: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:292 — `"shadowplay": [{ targets: [{ kind: 'skill', detail: 'acrobatics' }], when: "Tumble Through the opponent's space after a damaging melee Strike", bonus: "+2 circumstance" }]`.
