problem: Internally inconsistent with the batch's own ally-grant rule, and the authored entry would produce a wrong star. The text is "When you successfully Treat a Disease on someone and they fully recover from the disease, they gain a +2 circumstance bonus to saving throws against that same disease for 1 week" — the beneficiary is the patient, and the spec's own engineNote says "a star on the owner's own saves is usually wrong". Yet it still authors `targetKind: 'save', save: 'all'`, which (unlike root-magic and hasty-celebration in the very same batch, where the ally-only reading correctly produced no `bonuses` at all) would light up the owner's Fortitude, Reflex AND Will with a bonus that in play almost always lands on someone else, against one named disease.
correction: Drop the `bonuses` array and keep `situational: true, needsEngineWork: true` with the ally-grant note, matching how root-magic and hasty-celebration were handled — nothing should be written into FEAT_SITUATIONAL for this feat until an ally-grant lane exists. If the owner treating themselves is judged worth surfacing, the honest place is a Medicine-skill reminder, not a star on all three saves. Either way, add `needsHumanDecision: true` with the same question the spec already asks for medic-dedication.

problem: The condition is misstated in a way that inverts who needs the feat, and it silently merges a branch that does not apply to you. The record reads: "When you Treat a Disease or a Poison, or someone else uses one of these actions on you, increase the circumstance bonus granted on a success to +4". The spec's `when` says "...or someone with this feat treats you" — the text imposes no such requirement on the treater. YOUR feat upgrades the bonus YOU receive from anyone's treatment. Conversely, the other branch ("when you Treat a Disease or a Poison") upgrades the bonus for the PATIENT you treated, i.e. another character — so it is not self-applicable at all and must not be part of the condition on your own save star.
correction: Keep situational:true, one entry, targetKind 'save', save 'all', bonus "+4 circumstance (instead of the usual +2)". Replace the `when` with: "on saves against a disease or poison you were Treated for — whenever anyone uses Treat a Disease or Treat a Poison on you (your feat raises the bonus from +2 to +4)". Add to the engineNote that the mirror-image branch — the +4 you confer on someone else when YOU Treat a Disease/Poison — targets another character's save and is not representable, in addition to the existing (correct) note that the success→critical success upgrade is a degree-of-success change with no representation.

problem: The two split entries are correct in target, but each one's condition is broadened to all four skills, which introduces a rules error the record does not contain. The record says only "You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your defenses against Deception, Diplomacy, Intimidation, and Performance checks" — it names no DCs. The spec's inference that Deception is opposed by Perception DC and Diplomacy/Intimidation/Performance by Will DC is right, but it then repeats the full four-skill list on BOTH entries. A player reading "to your Perception DC when a creature uses ... Intimidation ... against you" would conclude Demoralize targets Perception DC, and "to your Will DC when a creature uses Deception ... against you" would suggest Lie targets Will DC. Neither is true.
correction: Keep both entries, both +1 circumstance, needsEngineWork true (it is a DC bonus, not a roll bonus — the app has no DC kind). Narrow each `when` to the actions that actually oppose that DC: perception entry → "to your Perception DC when a creature uses Deception against you (Lie, Feint, Create a Diversion, Impersonate)"; save/will entry → "to your Will DC when a creature uses Diplomacy, Intimidation, or Performance against you (Make an Impression, Request, Demoralize, Perform)". Keep confidence medium and keep the existing note that the record names no DCs, so the split is an inference the app owner should confirm.

problem: The bonus entry itself is right (+1 status, Acrobatics, while in an aerial form that sets a specific Acrobatics modifier), but the engineNote invents a restriction the text does not contain: "Only applies on top of the form's replacement Acrobatics modifier, not on top of the character's own." The feat says only "Whenever you use *aerial form* to gain a form that grants you a specific Acrobatics modifier, you gain a +1 status bonus to Acrobatics checks" — it never conditions the bonus on which modifier you end up rolling. Aerial Form's own text in core.json reads "Acrobatics modifiers of +16, unless your own modifier is higher", so a high-Acrobatics character keeps their own modifier and still gets the +1. Baking the invented caveat into the condition text would tell a player at the table not to apply a bonus they actually have.
correction: Drop the engineNote's second clause. Keep the entry as: targets [{kind:'skill', detail:'acrobatics'}], bonus '+1 status', when 'while polymorphed by *aerial form* into a form that grants a specific Acrobatics modifier' — with no claim about whose modifier is used.

problem: The condition is narrowed beyond the text. The spec's 'when' says the bonuses apply "if the creature fails its save against your DC" — but the record grants the +2 on BOTH degrees in the middle: "**Success** ... If your AC is being targeted, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your AC. If you need to attempt a saving throw, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to the save." and "**Failure** ... you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your AC, and a critical hit against you becomes a normal hit ... a +2 circumstance bonus to the save, and if you critically fail, you fail instead." As written the player would think a Success on the enemy's save gives them nothing. The Mythic Point cost is also omitted from the condition.
correction: Keep both entries (+2 circumstance, targetKind ac / save 'all') but rewrite the 'when' as: "against the triggering single-target spell or ability, after you spend a Mythic Point and the creature's save against your class or spell DC is a success or a failure (no bonus on its critical success; on its critical failure the effect fails outright)". Only the defence the effect targets gets the bonus — that part of the note is right.

problem: needsEngineWork is set to true, but the engineNote itself correctly concludes that nothing should ever appear on this character's sheet: the record's only bonus ("For each range increment beyond the first, a creature gains a cumulative +2 circumstance bonus to their Reflex save") is granted to the CREATURES YOU SHOOT and is a drawback baked into the ability, not an ally/self stat the app is missing. Flagging engine work puts a phantom item on the 'features the engine still needs' backlog.
correction: Set needsEngineWork false (and situational false — there is no situational bonus to this character at all), keeping the engineNote text explaining that the +2 Reflex bonus belongs to the targets and is part of the ability's own resolution.

problem: needsHumanDecision is raised over whether the player picks one of the four skills, but the record has no choice language: "For the next 10 minutes, you gain a +2 status bonus to checks made using Acrobatics, Occultism, Stealth, or Survival." That is the standard PF2e phrasing for 'any check that uses one of these skills' (compare the same list-style wording in willing-runes and my-reputation-precedes-me); a per-use choice would read 'one of the following' or 'a skill of your choice'. The flag sends an unambiguous entry to the owner for review.
correction: Keep the four +2 status entries (acrobatics, occultism, stealth, survival) as authored and drop needsHumanDecision/question; confidence can be raised to high.

problem: The first bonus entry broadens the condition beyond the text. core.json reads: "you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude DC and saving throws against being confused, controlled, grabbed, immobilized, or restrained by that figure of authority for 24 hours". The phrase "against being confused, controlled, grabbed, immobilized, or restrained" governs BOTH "your Fortitude DC" and "saving throws" — it is a single prepositional phrase attached to the compound noun. The spec's entry 1 drops it entirely and reads "to your Fortitude DC against a figure of authority you critically succeeded at Lying to, for 24 hours", which a player would apply to every Fortitude DC against that person — Disarm, Trip, Shove, any Athletics maneuver — when RAW only covers the listed conditions. That is an invented broadening of exactly the kind flagged.
correction: Entry 1 'when' should be: "to your Fortitude DC against attempts by that figure of authority to make you grabbed, immobilized, or restrained, for 24 hours after you critically succeed at Lying to them" (save/fortitude, +1 circumstance — type and size are correct). Entry 2 is correct as written. This also answers the spec's own needsHumanDecision question: 'all' is right for entry 2 and needsHumanDecision should be false — the condition list is not a save-type list to be guessed at, it is the shared qualifier on both halves of the sentence, and it deliberately spans Will (confused/controlled) and Fort/Reflex (grabbed/immobilized/restrained). Narrowing entry 2 to Will would drop the grabbed/immobilized/restrained cases the text names explicitly.

problem: The saving-throw half of the feat is wrongly restricted to Fortitude and Reflex. The text is two sentences: "You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude or Reflex DC against attempts to reposition or shove you. This bonus also applies to saving throws against spells or effects that attempt to force you to move." The Fortitude-or-Reflex choice belongs ONLY to the DC sentence (that is the Reposition/Shove defence). The second sentence says "saving throws" with no save type at all. The spec folded it into the two DC entries as "and to Fortitude saves against effects that would force you to move" / "and to Reflex saves against ...", inventing a restriction the text does not state — so a Will save against a forced-movement effect (command and similar compulsions are Will) would show no marker at all.
correction: Keep the two DC entries but strip the invented save-type wording from them: "while in Anchor Stance (you must be in or under water): to your Fortitude DC against attempts to Reposition or Shove you" (save/fortitude) and the same for Reflex (save/reflex). Then add a THIRD entry: bonus "+2 circumstance", when "while in Anchor Stance (you must be in or under water): to saving throws against spells or effects that attempt to force you to move", targetKind 'save', save 'all'.

problem: A real, printed bonus is dropped from bonuses[] on a false premise. The text opens with "You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your initiative rolls for psychic duels" — that is a genuine typed circumstance bonus on the character's own roll, and it is the ONLY part of this feat that isn't gated on a mid-duel choice. The engineNote justifies omitting it with "there is no initiative stat in the list", which is factually wrong about this codebase: src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts already carries initiative bonuses under kind 'perception' ("all-this-has-happened-before" — "on your initiative roll (once per day)"; "swaggering-initiative" — "rolling initiative"; "ambush-awareness", "proximity-alert", "mediums-awareness"). So the record ends up with zero coverage for its least ambiguous benefit for a stated reason that does not hold.
correction: Either add an entry — bonus "+2 circumstance", when "on initiative rolls for psychic duels", targetKind 'perception' (matching the existing all-this-has-happened-before / swaggering-initiative precedent) — or, if it is held back, hold it back on the correct ground: rules/psychic-duels in core.json has an id and name but no description, so the data cannot confirm the duel's initiative roll is Perception-based, and filing it under perception could mark the wrong stat. Replace the 'no initiative stat' claim in engineNote with that. The rest of the spec stands: Mind Mace is correctly scoped to "during a psychic duel in which you chose Mind Mace" ("Each time you enter a psychic duel, choose one of the following benefits for the duration of that duel"), the spell-DAMAGE vs spell-attack/DC concern is real, Psychic Fist is correctly identified as a substitution, and the needsHumanDecision question about duel-only bonuses is legitimate.

problem: The condition adds a restriction the record does not contain. core.json's trigger is "An enemy makes a successful Disarm, Escape, Grapple, Shove, or Trip attempt" — full stop, no target named — and the body says "The next time you take the same action they did". The spec's 'when' says the enemy succeeded "against you". By RAW the feat also fires when you watch an enemy Grapple your ally or Escape from anyone; the spec's phrasing would tell a player at the table they had nothing, when they do. Low severity (it narrows rather than inflates) but it is still condition text that is not in the record.
correction: Change 'when' to: "to your Athletics check the next time you take the same action (Disarm, Escape, Grapple, Shove, or Trip) that an enemy just succeeded at; lost if you don't use it before the end of your next turn". Everything else is right — +1 circumstance, +2 if the enemy critically succeeded, skill/athletics, situational true.

problem: The spec's chosen default reading broadens two of the three bonuses far beyond what the text supports. Record text: "you gain a +1 item bonus to unarmed attack rolls, Acrobatics checks, and Reflex saves and DCs to Escape, Grab an Edge, or avoid falling prone." The spec reads the trailing qualifier as scoping ONLY the Reflex clause, so it emits an unqualified '+1 item on unarmed attack rolls' and an unqualified '+1 item on all Acrobatics checks' (condition text is only 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing'). Core.json's own action records show why that is the wrong default: `escape` says "Attempt a check using your unarmed attack modifier... You can attempt an Acrobatics or Athletics check instead", and `grab-an-edge` says "You must succeed at your choice of an Acrobatics check or a Reflex save". Each of the three listed statistics is exactly a legal roll for one or more of the three listed actions — that is why they are listed together, and the qualifier scopes the whole list. The spec's reading also hands a level-4 archetype feat a permanent +1 item bonus to every unarmed Strike (equivalent to a +1 striking weapon) and to every Acrobatics check, which the near-always-true 'while wearing your clothing' condition would then park behind a star as if it were rare.
correction: Keep needsHumanDecision, but flip the default to the narrow reading. All three entries should carry the Escape/Grab an Edge/avoid-falling-prone qualifier: strikeAttack — '+1 item', when: 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing, on unarmed attack rolls to Escape'; skill/acrobatics — '+1 item', when: 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing, to Escape, Grab an Edge, or avoid falling prone'; save/reflex — '+1 item', when: 'while wearing your sharkskin-trimmed clothing, to Grab an Edge or avoid falling prone (and to your Escape DC)'. Reword the question to: 'Does the trailing qualifier scope the whole list? The Escape and Grab an Edge action texts say each listed statistic is a legal roll for one of the listed actions, which is why I default to the narrow reading — confirm before we grant a blanket +1 item to unarmed attacks and Acrobatics.' Keep needsEngineWork for the Escape DC half.

problem: The condition was rewritten rather than recorded: the spec declares 'if the target is trained in that Lore' a Paizo typo for 'if you are trained in that Lore', then drops that whole branch from the condition text, leaving only 'if that Lore could identify it'. The record's actual text is "you can instead attempt a Lore check with a +2 circumstance bonus if the target is trained in that Lore or could be identified by that Lore when Recalling Knowledge" — two alternative branches joined by 'or'. The printed wording is not obviously a typo: a joke landing because the TARGET knows the subject (Blacksmithing Lore at a blacksmith) reads perfectly well for a feat literally called Dad Joke, and the second branch ('could be identified by that Lore') already covers the identification case, so the spec's rewrite makes the first branch redundant with the second. Emitting a condition that silently deletes half of a printed 'A or B' is the 'condition invented or broadened beyond what the text says' failure, in the narrowing direction. Secondary defect: target skill is 'lore', which is not a key the registry can match — situationalBonuses.ts documents skill detail as 'a skill key, a `lore:*` key, or `all`', so a bare 'lore' would match no skill and the star would never render.
correction: Set the when text to the printed rule, both branches: 'when you use Dad Joke and substitute a Lore check for the skill that would identify the target, if the target is trained in that Lore or could be identified by that Lore'. Move the typo hypothesis out of the data and into needsHumanDecision: 'The printed text says "if the target is trained in that Lore" — is that a Paizo typo for "if you are trained in that Lore", or does the target's own training genuinely qualify? I have kept the printed wording.' Keep needsEngineWork true and state the missing piece precisely: the registry has no 'any Lore' key (only concrete lore:* keys and 'all'), so skill:'lore' will not match anything as authored — either add an 'any lore' detail or use skill:'all' with the Lore-only condition spelled out.

problem: Invented/narrowed condition on the wearer's own bonus. The spec gates all three entries on "while you follow the order you issued". The record says: "Issue an order as part of the command. You and each ally within 60 feet who follows that order gain a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, damage rolls, and saving throws against fear until the beginning of your next turn." The restrictive clause "who follows that order" attaches to "each ally within 60 feet", not to "You" — the wearer, who issued the order, gains the bonus from the activation itself. Adding a follow-your-own-order requirement is a condition the text does not impose, and it would make a player think the star sometimes doesn't apply to them. Everything else in this spec is right: +1 status is the correct size/type, the ⟨1⟩ Command / once-per-day activation matches, and the "against fear" restriction on the saves half only (attack and damage unrestricted) is the correct reading — it mirrors the Inspire Courage wording. The needsEngineWork flag for the ally half and the needsHumanDecision question are both legitimate.
correction: Reword all three `when` fields to drop the follow-the-order clause, e.g. attack/damage: "for 1 round after you activate the epaulet (1/day) — until the beginning of your next turn"; save: "on saving throws against fear, for 1 round after you activate the epaulet (1/day) — until the beginning of your next turn". Keep situational true, +1 status, targets strikeAttack / strikeDamage / save(all), and keep needsEngineWork true for the 60-foot ally half.

problem: Incomplete, and internally inconsistent with how the same engineer treated acrobats-staff. All three cloak records carry an activated effect on a Diplomacy check that the spec omits entirely: "You wield your great stature to make a Request of a creature. If you roll a success on the check, you get a critical success instead." (major adds: "If you roll a critical failure on your Diplomacy check when you activate the cloak, you get a failure instead."), once/twice/three times per day respectively. For acrobats-staff the engineer DID list a non-numeric effect (the fortune reroll) as a registry entry and raised a human decision about it; here the equivalent non-numeric Diplomacy effect was silently dropped. The rest of the cloak specs is verified correct: +1/+2/+3 item to Diplomacy to Make an Impression, situational true, no passiveEffects on any of the three records so there is no double-count, and the reciprocal Gather-Information half genuinely has no representable target.
correction: Decide the non-numeric policy once and apply it to both items. If degree-shift/fortune effects belong in the registry (the acrobats-staff treatment), add a Diplomacy entry to each cloak: bonus "success becomes a critical success", when "once per day (twice for greater, three times for major), when you activate the cloak to make a Request" — and on cloak-of-repute-major only, add "a critical failure becomes a failure instead". If they do not belong, drop the acrobats-staff reroll entry instead. Fold this into the human-decision question already raised on acrobats-staff rather than answering it differently per item.

problem: The save target is narrowed to Fortitude, a restriction the text does not make. The record reads: "A polished pebble aeon stone imbues you with the strength of the earth, granting a +1 item bonus to saves and DCs against attempts to grapple or swallow you." It says "saves" and "DCs" plainly, with no save named. The spec's engineNote justifies the narrowing with "Grapple and Swallow Whole are resolved against your Fortitude DC rather than a save you roll" — but that reasoning only covers the DC half, and it invents a Fortitude-only restriction on the save half. Plenty of grab/swallow attempts arrive as spells or monster abilities that call for a Reflex or Will save, and those would silently lose the marker. The Foundry rule element for this exact item confirms the broad reading: selector ["saving-throw","fortitude-dc","reflex-dc","will-dc"], type item, value 1, predicated only on action:grapple / action:swallow-whole — i.e. ALL saves and ALL three save DCs, not Fortitude alone.
correction: Keep situational: true and the +1 item size, but change the target from save/fortitude to save/'all' (the registry's existing convention for "saves against X", as used by affliction-resistance, adaptive-vision, crown-of-the-master and this same engineer's staff-of-the-magi and olivine-pendeloque entries). Suggested entry: { bonus: '+1 item', when: 'on saves (and on your save DCs) against attempts to Grapple or Swallow you', target: { kind: 'save', save: 'all' } }. Leave needsEngineWork true — the DC half still has no target kind — and the needsHumanDecision question about "saves and DCs" anchoring is legitimate and should stand.

problem: needsEngineWork is set to FALSE, but the spec's own engineNote lists three gates it cannot express, and every one of the six bonuses is scoped to a specific creature ("against your hunted prey" / "when you Seek your prey"). The prompt names per-creature scope as an explicit needsEngineWork trigger, and the SAME reviewer correctly set needsEngineWork TRUE for amulet ("+2 status bonus to AC and saves against the target of your Exploit Vulnerability") and for adept-benefit-tome ("your next attack roll against that creature") for exactly this reason. Marked false, an engine consumer will render six unqualified stars (+4 Perception, +4 Survival, +4 Deception/Intimidation/Stealth, +2 AC) with no mechanism to scope them to the prey, to the Outwit edge, or to the per-skill master-proficiency gate. Separately, the spec enumerates what it deliberately left out ("Flurry's reduced multiple attack penalty and Precision's extra 1d8/2d8 precision damage are NOT typed bonuses and are correctly absent") but silently drops a third clause that IS a conditional modifier to a tracked stat: "When using a ranged weapon that you have master proficiency in, you can ignore the penalty if attacking your hunted prey within the weapon's second and third range increments." Ignoring the range-increment penalty is worth an effective +2/+4 on the attack roll and belongs on strikeAttack (the registry's `bonus` field explicitly permits "a short effect phrase").
correction: Set needsEngineWork TRUE, with the engineNote naming what is missing: (a) per-creature scoping — no way to say "only against your hunted prey"; (b) hunter's-edge gating — the last four entries apply only to Outwit and cannot be derived from this record's id; (c) per-skill/per-armor master-proficiency gating on each entry. All six bonus values themselves are CORRECT and confirmed: outwit's base is "+1 circumstance bonus to AC against your prey's attacks and a +2 circumstance bonus to Deception checks, Intimidation checks, Stealth checks, and any checks to Recall Knowledge about the prey", so the +2->+4 and +1->+2 upgrades are right, as is the replace-not-stack note. Add a seventh entry: { bonus: 'ignore the range increment penalty', when: 'when attacking your hunted prey within your ranged weapon's second or third range increment, if you have master proficiency in that weapon', targetKind: 'strikeAttack' } — or, if the app owner prefers to keep penalty-waivers out of the registry, say so explicitly in engineNote the way Flurry and Precision were handled, rather than omitting it silently.

problem: Rules error in the save split. The spec assigns "to resist a Disarm, Shove or Trip" to Reflex and only Grapple to Fortitude. In PF2e, Shove is Athletics vs the target's FORTITUDE DC (like Grapple); only Disarm and Trip target Reflex DC. As specced the star would land on the wrong defence for Shove.
correction: Fortitude entry: 'to resist a Grapple or Shove, while your divine spark is in this ikon'. Reflex entry: 'to resist a Disarm or Trip, while your divine spark is in this ikon'. Bonus and type (+1 circumstance) and the Athletics entry are correct; record text reads "you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks for these actions and to your saving throws to resist these actions".

problem: The third bonus entry ({targetKind:'perception', when:'granted to allies in the aura as well (same two conditions)'}) targets the CHARACTER's Perception a second time. The record says "You and your allies in the lantern's aura gain a +1 status bonus to visual Perception checks…" — one bonus, which entry 1 already covers. Registering it produces two near-identical stars on Perception.
correction: Delete the third entry. Keep exactly two: +1 status / perception (visual Perception to notice something inside the 20-foot aura) and +1 status / skill:'all' (Recall Knowledge about a creature in the aura). If the ally reach is worth recording, put it in the engineNote, not in bonuses.

problem: The omnidirectional-scan escalation is broadened beyond the text. The record says the +1 circumstance bonus "increase[s] to +2 ON THE ATTACK YOU'RE AIDING" (and +3/+4 on a critical success) — Aid always targets another creature's check, so the +2/+3/+4 can never apply to the character's own attack or damage. The spec's bonus string ('+1 circumstance (+2/+3/+4 if you then succeed…)') tells the player they may get +4 on their own roll.
correction: For the character's own sheet the omnidirectional-scan entries are a flat '+1 circumstance', when: 'against the creature you scanned with an amped omnidirectional scan, until the scan ends'. Move the +2/+3/+4 Aid escalation into the engineNote as an ally-facing effect. The detect-magic entry (+1 status to saves vs that source's magic for 3 rounds, +2 when the amp is heightened to 7th) is verified correct.

problem: The engineNote's premise is false, so the needsHumanDecision is moot. fire-gate DOES carry an effectChoices picker in core.json (id 'fire-gate-junction', options elemental-resistance / skill-junction / critical-blast / impulse-junction / aura-junction), and src/rules/build.ts explicitly records junction picks: "Record the pick even when the option carries no grant (a kineticist gate junction…)" into effectPicks. The app therefore already knows whether the Intimidation skill junction was taken.
correction: Drop the 'star an unselected junction with a caveat?' question for fire-gate and gate the entry on the recorded pick (effectPicks recordId 'fire-gate', choiceId 'fire-gate-junction', value 'skill-junction'). The bonus itself is right and is confirmed by the option's own note in core.json: "a +1 status bonus to Intimidation while your kinetic aura is active (+2 at 10th, +3 at 17th)".

problem: Two errors. (1) The impulse-junction condition is wrong: the kinetic-gate feature says a Single Gate kineticist "gain[s] an impulse junction" automatically for their element, and it triggers "when you use an impulse of the chosen element that takes 2 actions or more" — it is not an optional pick for a single-gate earth kineticist, and the spec's when ('after you use it') omits the 2-action requirement. (2) The engineNote's blanket claim that "the app does not record which junction was chosen" is wrong as a general statement (fire-gate has an effectChoices picker); what is true is that earth-gate specifically has NO effectChoices in core.json — a per-record data gap, not an engine gap.
correction: AC entry when: 'until the start of your next turn, after you use an earth impulse that takes 2 or more actions (automatic if earth is your single gate; otherwise only if you took the earth impulse junction)'. Athletics skill-junction entry and its +1/+2/+3 status ladder are correct. Reword the engineNote: earth-gate is missing the effectChoices junction picker that fire-gate already has, so the fix is to add the picker, not to build new engine support.

problem: Inherits earth-gate's false premise via "Same as earth-gate". Junction picks ARE tracked by the engine (build.ts effectPicks); metal-gate simply has no effectChoices block in core.json, unlike fire-gate.
correction: Keep the +1 status (+2/+3) Crafting entry as written, but restate the open item as a DATA gap: add a 'metal-gate-junction' effectChoices picker mirroring fire-gate's, then gate the entry on the recorded pick. Note also that the metal impulse junction (reactive damage) is automatic for a single-gate metal kineticist and fires on a 2+ action metal impulse.

problem: Both bonuses on this record are verbatim duplicates of separate features the same character also has. The Adept save bonus text is word-for-word identical to adept-benefit-shield ("you gain a status bonus to your saves against spells and other magic effects equal to your circumstance bonus to AC from your shield"), and the -1 AC-at-1-HP penalty is word-for-word initiate-benefit-shield, which is specced separately in this same chunk. As specced, a shield thaumaturge gets two stars on AC and a redundant one on saves.
correction: Register nothing on the 'shield' implement record itself (its Intensify Vulnerability text — shield HP regain / +Cha Hardness / ally sharing — contains no character-stat bonus). Put the status save bonus on adept-benefit-shield only, and the -1 circumstance AC penalty on initiate-benefit-shield only. The bonus TYPES are right and worth preserving: 'shield' adept is a STATUS bonus to saves, whereas sparkling-targe's is a CIRCUMSTANCE bonus — do not unify them.

problem: Flag inconsistency that will misdrive registration. This record yields zero character-facing bonuses (the +2 status goes to "that ally" adjacent to your familiar) yet is marked situational:true with an empty bonuses array — while paragon-benefit-shield, which is also purely ally-facing, is marked situational:false with reasonIfNot. One of the two conventions has to go.
correction: Set situational:false with reasonIfNot ('every modifier lands on an ally, not on the character; nothing on this sheet should be starred'), keeping needsEngineWork:true for a future party/ally-buff display. Same treatment for 'regalia'. The three eidolon records (construct-eidolon, devotion-phantom-eidolon, elemental-eidolon) are a different case and can stay situational:true, because the app does model the eidolon — their bonuses are real, just companion-scoped.

problem: Same situational:true-with-no-bonuses inconsistency as choir-politic (the Intensify Vulnerability +1/+2 circumstance goes to a chosen ALLY's attack rolls). Additionally the engineNote's inventory of where the content lives is incomplete: it names initiate-benefit-regalia and paragon-benefit-regalia, but adept-benefit-regalia also exists and carries substantial character-facing bonuses (Deception/Diplomacy/Intimidation rising to +2 with master proficiency; the +1 status save bonus widening from fear to ALL mental effects; +2/+3/+4 status to damage rolls for you and allies in the aura).
correction: Set situational:false with reasonIfNot (ally-only), needsEngineWork:true. Fix the engineNote to name all three sibling records, and flag adept-benefit-regalia as carrying unspecced character bonuses — notably a status bonus to damage rolls for the character themself, which is a strikeDamage-shaped entry nobody has claimed yet.

problem: needsEngineWork:true contradicts the spec's own (correct) engineNote. The two degree-of-success upgrades are already expressible: situationalBonuses.ts line 76 carries "breath-control": bonus "+1 circumstance", when "against inhaled threats (success becomes critical success)", i.e. prose in the bonus field is established practice. Nothing new is needed for the character-facing half.
correction: Set needsEngineWork:false (or scope it explicitly to the ally-facing Follow the Expert +3/+4 and the aura's flanking / condition-penalty reduction, which genuinely have no representable target). The two entries themselves are correct: Coerce is Intimidation, Make an Impression and Request are Diplomacy, and the record does say "If you roll a critical failure … you get a failure instead".

problem: The SECOND bonus is narrowed to Fortitude, which the text does not say. The record reads: "If the triggering poison was normal Alcohol, you instead automatically succeed at the triggering save and gain a +4 status bonus on saves against alcohol for 1 minute." — unqualified "saves", not "Fortitude saves". (The FIRST bonus is correctly Fortitude: that sentence does say "on the triggering Fortitude save and on Fortitude saves against the same poison".) This is also self-inconsistent with the same engineer's own venomous-cure-fulu note, which deliberately used save 'all' for exactly this reason — the trigger there names no save, so neither should this follow-on clause.
correction: Change the +4 entry's save from 'fortitude' to 'all', keeping when: "instead, if the triggering poison was ordinary alcohol — you auto-succeed at the triggering save and get +4 against alcohol for 1 minute". Leave the +2 entry as save 'fortitude'. Add an engineNote mirroring venomous-cure-fulu: alcohol's own save is Fortitude in practice, so a Fortitude-only flag would cover the common case but is narrower than the printed text.

problem: The second listed bonus — { bonus: "double Hit Points regained from resting", targetKind: "hp" } — is not a typed bonus to any stat and should not be a registry entry at all. Emitting it puts a star on the character's max-HP tile for something that multiplies overnight rest recovery. The spec is self-contradictory: it lists the entry and then says in engineNote "should be dropped rather than starred on max HP". A registry entry that the spec itself says to drop will still get written by anyone consuming the bonuses array.
correction: Delete that entry from bonuses. Keep only the +2 status save entry (which is correct: text says "a +2 status bonus to saves against mental effects that occur in your dreams", unqualified, so save 'all' is right). Keep needsEngineWork true and move the rest-recovery text entirely into engineNote as a capability gap ("nightly rest recovery has no stat surface"), so nothing renders for it.

problem: The Will-save entry's condition asserts a 1-minute duration the text does not grant. The record reads: "You gain a +1 status bonus to Will saves. Choose a weapon or an unarmed Strike; your chosen attack deals an extra 1d6 damage for the next 1 minute." The clause "for the next 1 minute" is attached to the extra damage sentence; the Will bonus sentence carries no duration. The spec's when text ("for 1 minute after Activating the oath") reads a duration into the record.
correction: Reword the Will entry's when to what the text supports, e.g. "after Activating the oath (⟨1⟩ command, once per day) — the printed text states no duration for the Will bonus", and set needsHumanDecision true with the question: "Oath of the Devoted prints the +1 status Will bonus with no duration; only the extra 1d6 is explicitly 'for the next 1 minute'. Should the app display the Will bonus as also lasting 1 minute (the common reading), or as untimed?" The strikeDamage entry's 1-minute duration is correct and needs no change.

problem: All four pin the Learn a Spell bonus to skill 'arcana', but none of the four records names any skill — each says only "grants you a +N item bonus to checks to Learn a Spell if you do so by transcribing the spell into the grimoire", and the preparation clause is generic ("if you use the grimoire during your daily preparations and are capable of preparing spells of the appropriate rank"). Learn a Spell is rolled with the skill matching the SPELL'S tradition, so the target is caster-dependent, not fixed. The spec flags this in engineNote and sets confidence 'medium' but leaves needsHumanDecision false, which is the wrong disposition for a target the text does not support.
correction: Keep skill 'arcana' as the pragmatic default (grimoires are arcane prepared-caster gear, so it is right for the overwhelmingly common case, and skill 'all' would star every skill — strictly worse), but set needsHumanDecision true on all four with the question: "Endless Grimoire's Learn a Spell bonus names no skill; Learn a Spell uses the spell's tradition skill. Should the entry stay hard-coded to Arcana, or follow the character's spellcasting-tradition skill?" Bonus values themselves are all verified correct (+1 / +2 / +2 / +3).

problem: The bonus is scoped too broadly. The record says: "your Strikes with this scimitar that deal fire damage gain a +2 status bonus to their FIRE damage" — the +2/+3/+4 applies only to the fire component of the Strike, not to the Strike's whole damage. The spec's bonus field reads "+2 status" with a `when` of "on Strikes with this scimitar that deal fire damage", which a player at the table will read as +2 to the Strike's total damage. A flaming scimitar deals slashing plus a separate 1d6 fire, so the two are not the same number.
correction: Restate the first entry as bonus: "+2 status to the fire damage (+3 with greater striking, +4 with major striking)", when: "on the fire damage of Strikes with this scimitar, while you have a status bonus to at least one of your Speeds". Everything else in this spec is confirmed: targetKind strikeDamage, the Speed-status precondition, and the second entry (+10-foot status bonus to Speed until the end of your next turn, triggered when your spell deals fire damage) — activationCost is {"type":"free"}, so "free-action activation" is right, and there is no frequency limit on that activation.

problem: The reasonIfNot misquotes the gate and the chunk is internally inconsistent. The record says "CONSULTING the thesis grants a +2 item bonus to Warfare Lore checks. Like most scholarly compendiums, this usage requires holding the thesis in one hand." The spec claims "The only stated condition is holding the thesis in one hand" — but holding is the requirement OF consulting; the gating verb is the act of consulting the book, which is exactly the same class of "restricted to some uses of the skill" that the SAME engineer marked situational:true and raised as needsHumanDecision on violet-ray (Medicine limited to four actions) and nosoi-charm (Performance limited to instrument/orate/sing). Three near-identical patterns got two different verdicts.
correction: Do not assert unconditional on the strength of "only holding is required". Either (a) keep situational:false but set needsHumanDecision:true with the same question already asked on nosoi-charm/violet-ray — "does a bonus gated on actively consulting/using the item stay flat in passiveEffects, or come out of the maths?" — and quote "Consulting the thesis" as the evidence; or (b) if the answer to that question is "pull it out", this record must move with them. Confirmed facts: passiveEffects.skills['lore:warfare'] = 2, usage held-in-one-hand, traits [extradimensional, invested, magical], and the once-per-day 1-action unfurl grants no check bonus.

problem: The engineNote reverses the two records: it claims "An unsuffixed 'dragons-blood-pudding' umbrella record also exists" and that -lesser is merely contaminated. In core.json it is the opposite. `dragons-blood-pudding-lesser` (level 2, 5 gp, NO `usage` field, no consumableType/uses) IS the family blob — its description is the whole Grand Bazaar entry, all four grades, ending with the +2/+3/+4 Intimidation lines. The unsuffixed `dragons-blood-pudding` is the CLEAN single-grade record: level 2, 5 gp, usage held-in-one-hand, consumableType + uses fields, text reading "attempts a counteract check with a +6 counteract modifier" and containing no quickened clause and no Intimidation bonus. The evidence gloss "the lesser grade this record covers" is also wrong — this record covers all four grades. This matters because it points the umbrella-record policy decision at the wrong id: skipping the unsuffixed record here would delete the only clean lesser-grade entry, while the actually-contaminated -lesser record would be kept.
correction: Verdict stays situational:false (correct — the lesser grade only grants a counteract check, no character-stat bonus). Rewrite the note: `dragons-blood-pudding-lesser` is the family blob (no usage field, all four grades in one description); the unsuffixed `dragons-blood-pudding` is the clean, priced, single-grade record and is the one to keep. Note that this family's blob/clean split is INVERTED relative to sulfur-bomb, vexing-vapor and malleable-mixture, where the unsuffixed id is the blob — so any 'skip unsuffixed ids' rule would be wrong here.

problem: The second bonus entry ("+4 circumstance to AC while you Raise this tower shield and Take Cover behind it", targetKind ac) should not be in the list, and its condition is broadened. The record's own line is "AC increases to +4 if you are using the Take Cover action" — it conditions on Take Cover only, not on "while you Raise this shield", and it is the boilerplate tower-shield line reprinted in every tower shield's stat block, not a property of this magic item. core.json already models the shield mechanically (itemType 'shield', acBonus 2, hardness 9, hp 54, bt 27), so the +4 is the generic greater-cover result that REPLACES the shield's +2 (both circumstance, they do not stack) — the spec's "instead of the usual +2" is right on that point, but attaching it as an item-specific star would put an AC marker on this one shield while every other tower shield shows none.
correction: Drop the AC entry; keep only the demon-saves entry: +2 circumstance, targetKind save, save 'all', when 'while this shield is raised, on saves against demons' innate spells and special abilities' (that clause is verbatim in the record and correctly typed as circumstance). If the owner wants Take Cover surfaced at all, it belongs in the tower-shield/shield engine as a universal rule, not in the per-item situational registry. The ally-cover clause is correctly left unencoded (no target kind for another character's saves).

problem: Minor evidence defect, same class as the pudding one: the gloss says "the lesser grade this record covers grants no item bonus at all". problem: Classification is right (+1 item, visual Perception only) but needsEngineWork:false is wrong, and the engineNote ("must not be folded into the total") is contradicted by the record itself: core.json items['eye-of-the-unseen'].passiveEffects = {"perception":1}, so the app ALREADY adds the sight-only +1 to the unconditional Perception total. problem: needsEngineWork:false is wrong. problem: needsEngineWork:false is wrong and the stated reason for skill 'lore:*' is a misreading. The registry doc comment ("a skill key (e.g. intimidation), a `lore:*` key, or `all`") means a key of the lore:<subject> family (ProficiencyKey = SkillId | `lore:${string}` in src/rules/types.ts), not a literal wildcard. targetMatches (situationalBonuses.ts:376) is `t.detail === 'all' || t.detail === ref.skill` — there is no wildcard branch, so a literal 'lore:*' matches no skill and the entry would be silently dead (no star ever). problem: The condition string misstates the timing: "while Stage 1 of plasma hype is active (1 round after you Interact to take it)" reads as a one-round delay before the bonus arrives. problem: Two problems, both silent decisions that were not escalated. (2) Add { bonus: 'DC 5 flat check or the spell fails', when: 'whenever you Cast a Spell while wearing noqual armor', target: { kind: 'spell' } } — the registry's prose/penalty precedent (barbarian-dedication line 69) supports it, and a caster in noqual armor needs that flag more than the +1 AC. problem: needsEngineWork is set to true, but nothing on this record needs engine work for the situational-bonus feature. Keep the single bonus entry unchanged (+1 item, when: 'on Recall Knowledge checks made while using the Investigate exploration activity, with the lens activated', target { kind: 'skill', skill: 'all' }), and demote the initiative-substitution clause to a prose/engineNote observation rather than a blocking flag.

problem: needsHumanDecision:true with the question "Does the situational registry's `save` target accept 'all', or must every save bonus be pinned to fortitude/reflex/will?" — that question is already answered in the code the spec was matching. src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts documents SituationalTarget.detail as "For `save`: `fortitude` | `reflex` | `will` | `all`", and targetMatches() implements `t.detail === 'all'` as a wildcard. problem: The engine note claims the initiative reroll is "scoped to initiative - the app has no initiative target, so mapping it onto Perception is an approximation that over-reports if the character rolls initiative with a skill". problem: Two problems. problem: The second bonus entry uses skill key "lore" (bare). Verified against the registry contract: SituationalTarget.detail for kind 'skill' is documented as "a skill key (e.g. `intimidation`), a `lore:*` key, or `all`", and targetMatches() in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts compares with strict equality (`t.detail === ref.skill`). problem: needsEngineWork is set to false on all six canary records (canary, canary-informant-basic-services, canary-informant-advanced-services, canary-tail-first-week/second/third/fourth), but the entries can never fire. characterSituationalIds() in src/rules/explain.ts only admits an inventory row when `inv.equipped || inv.worn || inv.invested` ("An ITEM only counts while it is actually in use").
