The bonus text itself is quoted accurately and the Gather Information → Diplomacy mapping and the +1/+2 circumstance types are correct.
correction: Set needsEngineWork true on all six canary records with the note: hireling/service items have no equipped/worn/invested state, so the current item gating in characterSituationalIds() will never surface them; they need either a "service is active" flag on the inventory row or a separate non-item lane. This also makes the existing needsHumanDecision question concrete — today the answer is moot because nothing would display either way.

problem: situational is true while bonuses is an empty array — a self-contradicting shape. The record text is quoted correctly and the reasoning is right ("treat critically failed checks made to Aid as regular failures instead" is a degree-of-success shift with no numeric modifier, and "the circumstance bonus you provide for succeeding or critically succeeding at checks to Aid increases by 1" boosts what ANOTHER creature receives), but a downstream applier that keys off `situational === true` will emit `'the-publican': []`, an entry that stars nothing and reads as an authoring mistake later.
correction: Either set situational false with the existing explanation moved into reasonIfNot (nothing on this card is a bonus to one of your own stats), or keep situational true only if the project's convention is "situational but unrepresentable" — and state that convention explicitly. Keep needsEngineWork true and the human-decision question either way; do not leave true + empty as-is.

problem: Under-coverage. The standing bonus is captured correctly ("grants you a +1 status bonus to attack rolls you make as a readied action" → strikeAttack, +1 status), but the activation was dismissed as "a fortune effect, not a standing bonus". The record's Effect reads "Reroll the triggering Strike with a +1 status bonus" — the fortune part is the reroll; the +1 status is a separate, genuinely situational typed bonus to an attack roll under a stated condition (Trigger: "You miss a creature with a melee weapon Strike", Frequency once per day), which is exactly what this registry is for.
correction: Add a second entry: bonus "+1 status", targetKind strikeAttack, when "on the once-per-day reroll after you miss a creature with a melee weapon Strike (Activate, reaction)". Low impact — the card already stars strikeAttack via the readied-action entry, so no star is lost, only the popup line.

problem: Marked situational:true (+1 item bonus to "one Lore skill") with needsEngineWork:true claiming "there is no fixed lore:<name> key to attach it to" and "the registry needs either a wildcard Lore target or a per-day 'ancestor's Lore' selection". Three things are wrong. (1) UNCONDITIONAL FLAGGED AS SITUATIONAL — the record reads "In addition, until the next visitation, you gain a +1 item bonus to one Lore skill related to the ancestor, as determined by the GM." There is no in-play condition: once the Lore is known, the +1 applies to EVERY check with that skill. That is exactly the error class the brief warns about (a permanent bonus on a star misleads). Foundry corroborates: .import-src/pf2e/packs/pf2e/equipment/ancestral-geometry.json prints the same sentence with no predicate. (2) The engine gap does not exist. The core.json record already ships effectChoices: [{ id: 'ancestor-lore', prompt: "Choose the ancestor's Lore skill (+1 item bonus, re-picked at daily preparations)", options: architecture/engineering/genealogy/labor/mining/warfare }], each option carrying grant.passive.skills['lore:<x>'] = 1 — and C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\build.ts resolves item effectChoices into resolvedItemPassives[itemId], applied by derive while the item is worn. So the bonus is ALREADY in the computed total; adding a star on top invites the player to double-count it. (3) Factual misread in the engineNote: it calls the Activate "the 5-action Activate". The record's activationCost is {"type":"reaction"} and carries a Trigger line ("You rolled a saving throw of the noted type"); the ⟨5⟩ in the description is the app's REACTION glyph (src/sheet/RichText.tsx maps '5' -> 'Reaction'; src/sheet/AstRenderer.tsx maps reaction -> '5').
correction: Set situational:false. reasonIfNot: "The +1 item bonus applies to every check with the ancestor's chosen Lore until the next daily preparations — no in-play condition — so it belongs in the computed Lore total, not on a star. core.json already models it: the record's effectChoices ('ancestor-lore') carry grant.passive.skills['lore:<x>']=1 per option, which build.ts applies via resolvedItemPassives while the tattoo is worn, so a situational entry here would double-report it. The reaction Activate (replace the triggering save with the pre-recorded 2d20-keep-highest result) is a fortune reroll, not a bonus — no target kind, do not star a save." Set needsEngineWork:false. Drop the bonuses array. Optional data note for the owner (not a bonus issue): the picker offers six Lores but the printed text also allows "Lore about a dwarven deity", so the option list is narrower than the item permits.

problem: The `when` text and the evidence both call the triggered activation a "5-action activation" / "5 actions". In core.json the description reads `**Activate** ⟨5⟩ (concentrate)` and `src/sheet/widgets.tsx` maps glyph char "5" to a REACTION (char "4" = free action, only 1-3 are literal action counts). A 5-action cost is impossible in PF2e, and this string is printed to the player at the table. Secondary: the text is "a +1 status bonus to AC and saving throws and a +2 status bonus against mental effects" — the +2 is parallel to "AC and saving throws", so restricting it to saves only is a narrowing the sentence does not support.
correction: Reword both `when` strings to "until the start of your next turn after Activating the jar (reaction, once per hour) — triggered by a critical success on an attack roll with a witch spell, or a target critically failing its save against your witch spell or hex". Consider adding a fourth entry `{bonus:'+2 status', when:'against mental effects, until the start of your next turn after that activation', targetKind:'ac'}` alongside the save entry, or flag the AC/save scope of the +2 as needsHumanDecision. Everything else in this spec is confirmed: the trigger wording, the +1 status AC/saves, the unconditional +2 item bonus to the patron skill (hexing-jar has NO passiveEffects/dynamicSkillBonus in core.json, so that gap is real), and the unrepresentable familiar half.

problem: `when` says "if you spend the glaive's 4-action activation to listen to it". The record reads `**Activate** ⟨4⟩ (concentrate)` and glyph "4" is a FREE ACTION per src/sheet/widgets.tsx, not four actions. It also has a Trigger, which confirms it is not a 4-action activity.
correction: Change `when` to "on an Occultism check to Decipher Writing, Identify Magic, Learn a Spell, or Recall Knowledge, if you Activate the glaive (free action) to listen to it". The +4 item bonus, the target (skill/occultism), and the four listed uses are all confirmed correct.

problem: Marked situational:true, but the deity clause is exactly the same all-or-nothing eligibility gate this same engineer correctly classified as situational:false on cloister-robe ("The robe doesn't grant any benefits to a wearer who doesn't worship the deity tied to the robe"). The cassock text is "While you remain loyal to another deity, you believe the cassock grants you a +2 item bonus... It does neither... If you convert to following the cassock's true unholy deity, however, these bonuses function normally for you." There are only two states: bonus absent entirely, or bonus permanent and unconditional. Neither is a per-check circumstance. Worse, flagging it situational makes the sheet print the condition text "only if you worship the cassock's true unholy deity" by default — which spoils the GM's secret, the very thing the spec's own needsHumanDecision asks about.
correction: Set situational:false with reasonIfNot "once you worship the cassock's true unholy deity the +2 item to Religion / +1 item to that deity's divine skill are permanent; while you worship anyone else they do not exist at all. Item-level eligibility gate, not a per-roll condition." Keep needsHumanDecision (cursed-item display policy) and keep the engineNote about the suppression rule and the dynamic divine skill — both are accurate. Note core.json already has a `dynamicSkillBonus: {source: 'bloodline'|'deity', value}` lane wired into src/rules/derive.ts line 244, which is the natural home for the deity-skill half.

problem: The needsHumanDecision question rests on a false premise. It asks whether the crown "should carry a player-facing material picker (like the Doubling Rings rune-copy picker) that drives a real item bonus, or stay display-only text". The core.json record ALREADY has `effectChoices: [{id:'crown-material', prompt:"Choose the crown's material (+1 item bonus)", options: antlers→intimidation 1 / flowers→diplomacy 1 / leaves→stealth 1}]`, i.e. the picker exists and already grants a real passive item bonus. Asking the owner to decide something already built wastes a decision cycle, and the question omits the part that IS unmodelled.
correction: Drop the picker question. The classification (situational:false) is correct and should stand. Replace the question with the real gap: the three effectChoices options hard-code +1, but the text says "If you invest and wear living mantle along with the crown, the crown's item bonus increases by 1" — living-mantle exists in core.json as its own invested item and nothing escalates the crown to +2 when both are invested. Also keep the druid-only investiture gate note ("You can invest this item only if you're a druid").

problem: The penalty entry's `when` reads "to Survival checks to Sense Direction or navigate, once the telescope has fused to you". The record says flatly "The telescope imposes a –4 circumstance penalty to Survival checks to Sense Direction or navigate." — there is no "once fused" qualifier on that sentence. Fusing is described in the preceding sentence about using another device to observe stars ("Once you use it, it fuses to you, and you must succeed at a save to use another device to observe the stars"), and the spec has carried that qualifier across into an unrelated clause. This is a condition invented beyond the text, and it materially understates the curse (a player who has not yet activated it would think they are unaffected).
correction: Change `when` to "to Survival checks to Sense Direction or navigate, while you have the telescope" (no fusion gate). Keep the needsHumanDecision about whether penalties belong in this bonus registry — that question is legitimate. The +2 item entry (skill/occultism, on checks to observe the night sky) and the note that the Occultism-for-Perception substitution is unrepresentable are both confirmed correct.

problem: Invalid target detail. The spec emits `targetKind: "skill", skill: "lore"`, but `lore` is not a value the registry can resolve. The real contract in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts documents `SituationalTarget.detail` for kind `skill` as "a skill key (e.g. `intimidation`), a `lore:*` key, or `all` (any skill)" — there is no bare `lore` skill. The engineNote also claims "existing registry precedent uses detail 'lore:*'"; that is false — I scanned all 416 lines and NO entry uses a `lore:` detail (it exists only in the doc comment). As written this entry would silently match nothing, so the star never appears — the exact bug this whole effort is meant to fix.
correction: Keep situational: true and the +2/+3 item bonus (text confirmed verbatim: "you gain a +2 item bonus to Lore checks made to Recall Knowledge ... This increases to a +3 bonus if you are at least 17th level"). Change the first entry's target to a resolvable one — either fan out to one entry per Lore the character actually has (`skill`/`lore:<name>`), or use `skill`/`all` with the condition text carrying the restriction: when = "to Recall Knowledge, but only with a Lore skill". Do not leave `skill: "lore"`.

problem: Missing a target. The record says the activation grants "a +1 circumstance bonus to attack rolls against the creature and to your AC and saving throws against attacks and effects from the creature". "Attack rolls" in PF2e includes SPELL attack rolls, not just Strikes. The spec emits only strikeAttack, ac and save/all — so a caster (the exact character who wears an Intelligence apex item and studies a foe) gets no marker on the one stat they actually roll. The prompt's target list includes `spell`, so no invention is required.
correction: Add a fourth entry: { bonus: "+1 circumstance (+2 if you critically succeeded the Recall Knowledge)", when: "for 1 minute, on spell attack rolls against the creature you studied with the 1-action activation", targetKind: "spell" }. Everything else in this spec is confirmed correct, including that the +3 item bonus to Society is unconditional (passiveEffects.skills.society = 3 verified) and must not be starred.

problem: The classification (situational: false) is CORRECT and should stand — but the stated justification is factually wrong and should not be relied on. The spec says "The record already carries passiveEffects.skills.medicine = 3, so the engine folds it in." The record's text is "+2 item bonus to Medicine checks. This increases to a +3 bonus if you are at least 17th level", yet passiveEffects hardcodes a flat 3 with no level gate. A character below 17th level holding this artifact gets +3 where the rules give +2 — the engine does NOT fold it in correctly, it over-grants. (Verified this is unique among the unconditional items in this batch: bangles-of-crowns/intimidation:3, bracers-of-hammers/athletics:3, coronet-of-stars/medicine:3, cowl-of-keys/stealth:3, sash-of-books/society:3 are all flat +3 in their own text and so are correct; only the-midwife scales by level. passiveEffects demonstrably supports level formulas — the-cricket uses "10 + 10*floor(@actor.level/19)".)
correction: Keep situational: false. Drop the claim that the engine handles it, and instead flag the underlying data bug: passiveEffects.skills.medicine should be a level-gated formula (e.g. 2 + floor(@actor.level/17) style, matching the-cricket's pattern) rather than the constant 3. Same latent risk applies to the-dance and the-eclipse, which the spec correctly notes carry NO passiveEffects block at all (confirmed) and so currently grant nothing.

problem: The classification (situational false — "+1 item bonus to Stealth checks while wearing the armor" is unconditional) is CORRECT, but the spec's engineNote is factually wrong: it claims "The record already carries passiveEffects.skills.stealth: 1, so the engine folds it into the maths" and sets needsEngineWork false. It does not. Shadow is a PROPERTY rune. planRune() in src/rules/attachments.ts returns `{ ok: true, action: 'etch', ..., consume: true }` and stores only the rune id in `hostInv.runes.property` (line 128) while consuming the rune's inventory entry. passiveItemBonus() in src/rules/derive.ts (lines 205-226) — and the resolvedItemPassives lane at line 223 — iterate `c.inventory` only (`for (const inv of c.inventory) { if (!(inv.worn || inv.invested || inv.equipped)) continue; read(db.items[inv.itemId]?.passiveEffects); }`), so an etched rune id is never resolved back to its item definition. The ONLY consumers of `runes.property` anywhere in src/ are the damage-rider lanes (derive.ts lines 1236 and 1443, companions.ts line 730). Result: the shadow rune's +1 item bonus to Stealth is silently dropped from the Stealth total. Note the contrast the spec missed: potency/striking/resilient/reinforcing are stored as TYPED fields on inv.runes and ARE read (acItem at derive.ts line 419, resilientSaveBonus at line 158), which is why the armor-potency and resilient specs' engine claims are correct while this one is not.
correction: Keep situational: false (it is unconditional and belongs in the maths, not on a star). Change needsEngineWork to true with the note: GAP — passiveEffects on a PROPERTY rune are unreachable. Etching consumes the rune item (attachments.ts planRune, consume: true) and keeps only its id in inv.runes.property, but passiveItemBonus (derive.ts ~line 205) reads passiveEffects from inventory items only, so shadow's +1 item Stealth never lands. Fix: have derive.ts resolve each `(worn.inv.runes as ArmorRunes).property` id through db.items[...].passiveEffects and feed it into the same passiveItemBonus pool (still highest-wins, since item bonuses don't stack). The same lane is what any other passiveEffects-bearing property rune would need.

problem: Marked situational:false for the Performance bonus, with the reasoning that '+2 item bonus to Performance checks attempted while using it' is UNCONDITIONAL and 'must NOT also be starred'. That is the inflating-error direction. The clause 'attempted while using it' is a per-check condition, not an equipment state: a bard who Performs by singing, dancing, acting or oratory while the guitar hangs on their back gets nothing. Confirmed against the pristine AoN text too ('a virtuoso handheld musical instrument that grants a +2 item bonus to Performance checks attempted while using it'). Worse, core.json already carries passiveEffects.skills.performance = 2, and src/rules/derive.ts:220-224 applies passiveEffects.skills to EVERY check of that skill for any item that is merely worn/invested/equipped — so today the app adds +2 to all Performance checks, including ones made with no instrument at all.
correction: Keep the Chord of Protection AC entry as written (+2 status to AC vs the triggering melee attack, reaction, once per day — AoN confirms the once-per-day frequency). ADD a second entry for the instrument bonus instead of suppressing it: { bonus: '+2 item', when: 'on Performance checks made while actually playing the guitar (held in two hands) — not on Performance checks that do not use the instrument', targetKind: 'skill', skill: 'performance' }, and set needsEngineWork/needsHumanDecision so the owner decides whether to strip passiveEffects.skills.performance from the item record. Leaving it in the flat maths is the bug the mandate is trying to avoid. Same reasoning would apply to any other 'virtuoso instrument' record folded into passiveEffects.

problem: The 'when' string invents a frequency: '...if you use the teardrop's Reflect Emotions reaction (once per day)'. The record's own description puts 'Frequency once per day' under the FIRST activation (Request a Spell) only; Reflect Emotions lists a Trigger and nothing else. The pristine AoN text (aon-2e-archive equipment-2612.json) confirms: 'Activate—Reflect Emotions Reaction (concentrate) Trigger You're targeted by an emotion or metal effect; Effect You receive a +4 status bonus...' — no Frequency line. The single frequency object on the core.json record belongs to the 2-action Request a Spell activation (activationCost.value 2), not to the reaction.
correction: Drop the '(once per day)' clause. when: 'on the saving throw against an emotion or metal effect that targets you, if you spend the teardrop's Reflect Emotions reaction'. Everything else in this spec is correct: +4 status, save 'all' because the triggering effect picks the save, and the Perception +26 / Diplomacy +24 / Alchemy Lore +26 / Metal Lore +26 / Society +24 / Will +26 / Int +6 / Wis +2 / Cha +4 block is the intelligent item's own stat block and must not be imported (note the spec wrote 'Lore +26' — the record actually lists two Lores, Alchemy and Metal).

problem: Two flaws, both in how the size is expressed (the situational/target/type calls themselves are right). (1) The bonus field literally reads '+2 circumstance (the shield's own AC bonus)' — a player with a buckler would be shown +2 when the shield actually grants +1, which is exactly the 'wrong bonus size' failure the star is supposed to prevent; the note admits the size is variable but the displayed string still asserts +2. (2) The engineNote's worked example is factually wrong: it says '+3 for a tower shield behind cover'. A tower shield's circumstance bonus to AC is +2 raised, and Take Cover while it is raised increases that circumstance bonus to +4. There is no +3 case.
correction: Set bonus to a non-numeric formula string, e.g. 'equal to the raised shield's circumstance bonus to AC (+1 buckler, +2 most shields, +4 tower shield with Take Cover)', and have the display read the equipped shield's AC bonus rather than a literal. Fix the engineNote figure from +3 to +4 for a tower shield with Take Cover. The identical text and identical correction apply to keep-stone-shield-high-grade, whose description is byte-identical (it adds only Hardness 11 / HP 46 / BT 23 and the 13,200 gp price). The rest stands: save 'all' vs spells that target you while Raised, the '(as well as AC)' half is the ordinary Raise a Shield bonus and correctly not double-listed, and Shield Block vs spell damage is a capability not a bonus.

problem: The condition is NARROWED beyond the printed text. The record says: "Whenever a creature damages you with an attack, the skull changes its appearance to look like the face of that creature. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your next damage roll against that creature before the end of your next turn." — there is no clause limiting that damage roll to Strikes made WITH the axe. The spec's `when` reads "on your next damage roll with this axe against the creature that most recently damaged you", adding a restriction the text never states. A player reading the tooltip would wrongly conclude a Strike with a second weapon (or a spell's damage roll) is excluded.
correction: Word the trigger as printed: `when: "on your next damage roll against the creature that most recently damaged you with an attack, before the end of your next turn (while wielding the axe)"`. Keep bonus "+2 circumstance", targetKind strikeDamage, needsEngineWork true. If the app owner wants the axe-only reading enforced, that is a rules call, not something the text supports — set needsHumanDecision true with the question "Does the Retribution Axe's +2 circumstance damage bonus apply to any damage roll against that creature, or only to Strikes made with the axe?"

problem: Inconsistent needsEngineWork across four records that are the SAME case. acid-flask is marked needsEngineWork true ("the item bonus must be applied to the thrown bomb's own Strike, and it varies by grade"), but alchemists-fire, dread-ampoule and glue-bomb — verified identical in structure (each graded id is itemType "weapon", group "bomb", range 20, with "You gain a +1/+2/+3 item bonus to attack rolls" on moderate/greater/major and nothing on lesser) — are all marked needsEngineWork false. Any downstream pass that filters on needsEngineWork will pick up 1 of the 4 identical gaps and silently drop the other 3.
correction: Set the same flag and the same engineNote on all four catalog parents (acid-flask, alchemists-fire, dread-ampoule, glue-bomb) — either needsEngineWork true on all four ("per-bomb item bonus to attack rolls must be applied to that bomb's own Strike; Lesser +0, Moderate +1, Greater +2, Major +3") or false on all four if the strike engine already reads the graded records. The situational=false classification itself is correct for all four and should not change.

problem: INVENTED CONDITION. The spec's `when` is "...while wielding the staff", but the record's text contains no wielding requirement: "A *staff of healing* grants a +1 item bonus to the Hit Points you restore anytime you cast the *heal* spell using your own spell slots or charges from the staff." The word "wield"/"hold" never appears in this record (unlike every other staff in this chunk, which all print an explicit "While wielding the staff" clause — the contrast is deliberate, since the bonus is meant to apply to heal cast from your OWN slots). Adding the clause narrows the bonus to a state the text does not require and will tell a player at the table they lose it when the staff is stowed.
correction: Drop "while wielding the staff". `when`: "to the Hit Points restored whenever you cast heal using your own spell slots or the staff's charges". If the app owner wants a holding requirement it is a rules interpretation, not something the record says — raise it as needsHumanDecision, do not bake it into the condition. Separately: targetKind 'spell' should carry needsHumanDecision true as well, because 'spell' stars the spell attack/DC, a stat this item does not modify at all — a wrong star is worse than no star until a heal-amount target kind exists.

problem: Same invented "while wielding the staff" condition. Record text: "A *staff of healing* grants a +2 item bonus to the Hit Points you restore anytime you cast the *heal* spell using your own spell slots or charges from the staff." No wielding/holding clause anywhere in the description.
correction: `when`: "to the Hit Points restored whenever you cast heal using your own spell slots or the staff's charges" (+2 item). Same needsHumanDecision note on the 'spell' placeholder target as the base staff.

problem: Same invented "while wielding the staff" condition. Record text: "...grants a +3 item bonus to the Hit Points you restore anytime you cast the *heal* spell using your own spell slots or charges from the staff." No wielding/holding clause.
correction: `when`: "to the Hit Points restored whenever you cast heal using your own spell slots or the staff's charges" (+3 item). Same needsHumanDecision note on the 'spell' placeholder target.

problem: Same invented "while wielding the staff" condition. Record text: "...grants a +4 item bonus to the Hit Points you restore anytime you cast the *heal* spell using your own spell slots or charges from the staff." No wielding/holding clause.
correction: `when`: "to the Hit Points restored whenever you cast heal using your own spell slots or the staff's charges" (+4 item). Same needsHumanDecision note on the 'spell' placeholder target.

problem: The situational:false call and its reasoning are correct (the generic record's own text is boilerplate plus a concatenated dump of every variant), but the human-decision QUESTION states a false premise: it offers "split into the missing per-variant records first". No variants are missing. core.json already carries a separate item record for every variant named in the question and more: aeon-stone-amplifying, -consumed, -delaying, -envisioning, -peering, -nourishing, -preserving, -smoothing, -sprouting, -formulating, -repairing, -crescent, -vital-amplification, -flickering, plus the whole legacy colour-named set (aeon-stone-dusty-rose-prism, -pale-lavender-ellipsoid, etc.). Asking the owner about non-existent work wastes a decision and could trigger a pointless data task.
correction: Keep situational:false and the exclusion rationale. Rewrite the question to the real one: "Every aeon stone variant already exists as its own item record (aeon-stone-amplifying, -smoothing, -flickering, ... plus the legacy colour-named set), so the generic 'aeon-stone' parent should simply be excluded from the situational registry — confirm the aggregate record is never the one a character actually owns."

problem: The condition text invents an action type: "(activate as a reaction before rolling)". The record's activation is "**Activate** ⟨4⟩ (concentrate)" and its structured field is "activationCost": {"type": "free"}. In this app's own glyph mapping (src/sheet/RichText.tsx: '4': 'Free action'; src/sheet/widgets.tsx Glyph char="4" title="Free action'; AstRenderer.tsx 'free action': '4', reaction: '5'), ⟨4⟩ is a FREE action, not a reaction. Everything else in the spec (target save/will, +2 status, the 1-minute tail, excluding the degree-of-success upgrade) checks out.
correction: Change the when text to: "on the triggering Will save against fear and other saves against fear for 1 minute (free action, triggered when you attempt a Will save against a fear effect but haven't rolled yet)". Same caution applies to the sibling ⟨4⟩ talismans in this chunk (savior-spike, potency-crystal x3) — their spec text happens not to name an action type, so leave those alone, but do not later relabel them 'reaction' either.

problem: situational is true while bonuses is an empty array. The record text is confirmed correct ("your alchemical bomb Strikes reduce the circumstance bonus to AC your targets gain from cover", Lesser -1 / Greater -2) and the reasoning for granting no entries is right, but the classification flag contradicts it: a situational:true record with zero targets either produces a registry entry with no targets (an empty star popup on nothing) or gets silently dropped. Compare madcap-top in the same chunk, where the engineer used situational:false + reasonIfNot for the same 'nothing to star' outcome — the two records are flagged inconsistently.
correction: Set situational false with reasonIfNot: "The effect is conditional but is not a bonus to any stat of YOURS — it shrinks the target's cover circumstance bonus to AC. No allowed target kind fits ('ac' would be your AC; folding it into strikeAttack would be wrong because it only cancels cover, not a flat +1/+2)." Keep the existing engineNote and needsEngineWork:true so the gap is still recorded.

problem: The target is broadened past what the record says. Spec uses skill:'all' with the justification that "no single static skill key is right". But the text names a CLOSED list: "Choose one skill: Arcana, Crafting, Medicine, Nature, Occultism, Religion, Society, or a single subcategory of Lore." skill:'all' stars every skill on the sheet, including Athletics, Acrobatics, Stealth, Deception, Intimidation, Performance, Survival and Thievery, none of which the tome can ever be chosen for. (crown-of-intellect legitimately uses 'all' — its text literally says "regardless of the skill" — so the two records must not be encoded the same way.)
correction: Replace the single skill:'all' entry with the seven named skills plus Lore. The registry's SituationalBonus shape is targets: SituationalTarget[], so this is one bonus with seven-plus targets: [{kind:'skill',detail:'arcana'},{...'crafting'},{...'medicine'},{...'nature'},{...'occultism'},{...'religion'},{...'society'}] (plus the character's lore:* keys), when: "to Recall Knowledge with the one skill you chose when you Skimmed the tome, after spending an Interact action to peruse it (the pages last 24 hours)", bonus: "+3 item". Keep needsEngineWork:true only for the narrower ask — a per-activation chosen-skill selector so the star lands on the single chosen skill rather than all eight candidates.

problem: The engineNote's dedupe claim is incomplete and therefore misleading. It says this is "a misspelled duplicate of 'alacritous-horseshoes' ... whichever id the registry keys off, the other should be suppressed" — but core.json actually holds FOUR records for this item line: 'alacritous-horsehoes' (the misspelled variant-family record), 'alacritous-horseshoes' (base), 'alacritous-horseshoes-greater', and a third copy of the base, 'aon-alacritous-horsehoes' (also misspelled, empty price, no usage/edition fields). Suppressing only one of the two spares still leaves a duplicate star.
correction: Amend the note to name all three base-item records ('alacritous-horsehoes', 'alacritous-horseshoes', 'aon-alacritous-horsehoes') and state that the registry should key off the clean, priced record 'alacritous-horseshoes' with the other two suppressed. The bonus content itself (+2 circumstance to Athletics for High Jump and Long Jump, greater = +3) is verified correct against the text.

problem: The engineNote treats the Speed half as settled correct maths — "The +5-foot land Speed is unconditional and already in passiveEffects.speedBonus" (the same sentence appears on 'alacritous-horsehoes' and 'alacritous-horseshoes-greater'). It is unconditional, but it is mis-scoped in exactly the way the note flags for Athletics: the record reads "When you affix these ... to the hooves of an ordinary horse or a quadrupedal animal companion and the animal companion invests them, THAT CREATURE gains a +5-foot item bonus to its land Speed". passiveEffects.speedBonus = 5 (10 on the greater) applies it to the player character, so a PC carrying the shoes gets +5 ft Speed they are not entitled to. Marking that half 'already handled' will stop anyone from fixing it.
correction: Rewrite the note: "The +5-foot land Speed is unconditional but belongs to the COMPANION. core.json currently exposes it as passiveEffects.speedBonus = 5 (10 on the greater), which the engine applies to the PC — that is an inflated flat bonus, not correct maths. Both halves of this item (Speed and the Athletics jump bonus) need companion scoping." Apply the same correction to the notes on 'alacritous-horsehoes' and 'alacritous-horseshoes-greater'.

problem: The 5th listed bonus — {bonus: "Veil of Privacy (1 hour)", targetKind: "skill", skill: "deception"} — is invented. I read spells['veil-of-privacy'] in core.json: "You erect protective wards that make the target difficult to detect via magic. Veil of privacy attempts to counteract all detection, revelation, and scrying effects used against the target or the target's gear throughout the duration". It grants NO bonus to Deception or to any other stat, and it is not a typed bonus at all — the `bonus` field is a duration string, not a modifier. Starring Deception for it would tell a player they roll better on Deception during Cloak Identity, which is false. correction: Delete the 5th entry entirely. Keep only the four hood-up modifiers, all of which check out against the record text and against the item having no passiveEffects: +1 item Stealth, +1 item Deception restricted to Impersonating a forgettable background character, -1 item Diplomacy, -1 item Intimidation. Cloak Identity belongs to the activation/spell-effect lane (like Puff of Smoke on charlatan's-cape), not the situational-bonus registry. Note for the record that the base cloak's Veil of Privacy lasts 1 hour while the greater's is a 5th-rank version lasting 8 hours.

problem: The classification (situational false for both the +1 Intimidation and the +2 patron-skill bonus) is right, but the engineNote is factually wrong where it says the engine "needs a patron→granted-skill resolution (nothing in src/ references crown-of-witchcraft or a patron-skill lookup today)". The patron→skill mapping already exists in both data and code: core.json classes.witch.subclass.options[].grants.skills carries it for all 16 patrons (baba-yaga→occultism, choir-politic→society, faiths-flamekeeper→religion, the-inscribed-one→arcana, etc.), and src/rules/build.ts:1245-1247 already consumes subclass grant skills ("Subclass-/choice-granted skills (druid order, rogue racket, witch patron, eidolon)"). Useful safety fact while implementing: no patron grants Intimidation (all 16 grant arcana/nature/occultism/religion/society), so the crown's two item bonuses can never land on the same skill and the non-stacking-item-bonus case does not arise.

problem: Same defect as the base crown: the engineNote asserts a missing patron→skill lookup ("the +3 must resolve to the character's witch patron skill; the item cannot name it") as though the mapping were unavailable. problem: The reasonIfNot describes the engine as "effectiveWeaponRunes() (copies potency/striking onto the target weapon)", presenting the maths as already correct for this item. It is not: src/rules/derive.ts:924-928 returns `property: [...new Set([...(own?.property ?? []), ...(src.property ?? [])])]` unconditionally — the BASE rings copy property runes too, even though this record says only "the weapon's fundamental runes are replicated onto any melee weapon you wield in the hand wearing the iron ring" and reserves property-rune replication for the greater version ("The rings also replicate property runes..."). So the justification for 'no star needed, the maths already handles it' rests on a description of the code that is wrong in the player's favour.
correction: Keep situational: false (this is variable rune replication, not a fixed typed bonus — correct call). Fix the engineNote to state two engine defects, not one: (1) effectiveWeaponRunes does not gate the property-rune union on rings.greater, so base doubling rings over-grant property runes; (2) the same-weapon-group requirement enforced at derive.ts:919 for the base rings appears nowhere in either record's printed text — I re-read both descriptions and neither mentions weapon groups. The greater-rings spec's observation that the two property-rune provisos ('meets all the prerequisites for a given rune', 'is not a specific weapon') are unchecked is confirmed correct.

problem: The engineNote asserts a data defect that does not exist: "the record's activationCost is 'free' while the description shows the reaction glyph — worth checking the importer separately." The glyph in the description is ⟨4⟩, which is the FREE-ACTION glyph, not the reaction glyph. Inferred across the whole items collection: ⟨4⟩ maps to activationCost.type 'free' in 300 records and ⟨5⟩ maps to 'reaction' in 267 (e.g. sparkwarden 'Activate ⟨5⟩ envision' -> reaction; lionfish-spear 'Lionfish Poison ⟨5⟩' -> reaction). The record is internally consistent and matches the printed free-action talisman activation.
correction: Drop the importer aside entirely. The classification itself is right and unchanged: situational true, one row, +2 status, targetKind 'save', save 'fortitude', when 'on the Fortitude save against the INITIAL exposure to a disease or poison, when you activate the pin affixed to your armor (single use; a critical failure on the triggering roll becomes a failure)'. Keep needsHumanDecision for the consumable policy.

problem: The +10/+20/+30/+40 status bonus to Speed is dropped with no row on the grounds that it is "UNCONDITIONAL for the mutagen's duration — a timed effect for the maths/Modes lane". correction: Add a second row to the family record: bonus '+10 to +40 status (lesser/moderate/greater/major)', targetKind 'speed', when 'while the Prey Mutagen is active (1 minute to 1 hour by grade)'. Separately, the AC row's bonus string '+1 to +4 circumstance (lesser/moderate/greater/major)' is not a parseable modifier for a single record — on the family/summary record state the range in `when` and keep `bonus` to a single value or mark the record summary-only. Fold the Speed bonus into the consumable-policy question rather than silently dropping it.

problem: Same omission at grade level: "You gain a +10 status bonus to your speed" (verified verbatim in the record) is dropped as "unconditional for the duration", while the AC row from the same one-shot elixir is authored. problem: Two faults. (1) The engineNote claims "No authorable rows", but one clause is authorable and lands on the PC: "Creatures in the aura and in the same body of water as the ship take a -2 circumstance penalty to Athletics checks to Swim." The Lash Out! aura is centred on YOUR OWN ship (emanation equal to the ship's length), so a PC or ally swimming beside their own ship is inside it. The note's claim that the Swim penalty lands "on arbitrary creatures in the aura ... not on the item's owner" is an overstatement — the aura does not exclude your own crew. The registry already accepts penalties (two negative entries exist). (2) The row is under-specified: situational is set to true but the object carries neither a `bonuses` array nor a `reasonIfNot`, so it asserts a situational bonus exists while yielding nothing to display and no stated reason.

Correct the engineNote to say the Swim penalty CAN hit the owner and their party. If the intent was that nothing is authorable, the row must carry reasonIfNot rather than a bare situational:true.

problem: Identical to the base figurehead, whose text this record repeats verbatim: the -2 circumstance penalty to Athletics checks to Swim inside the Lash Out! aura is authorable and can land on the PC (the aura is on your own ship), so "Same gap as kraken-figurehead" / no authorable rows is wrong; and the row sets situational:true with neither a `bonuses` array nor a `reasonIfNot`.
correction: Same as the base record: add bonus '-2 circumstance', targetKind 'skill', skill 'athletics', when 'to Athletics checks to Swim while you are in the water inside your ship's Lash Out! tentacle aura'. Keep needsEngineWork true for the Board check and piloting penalties only. (The rest of the spec is accurate: this grade differs only by 7d10 hull damage and the DC 31 break-free check.)

problem: The situational:true call is right (Foundry predicates 'visual'), but the engineNote is wrong about what the app does today and hides a live inflation bug. core.json ALREADY carries passiveEffects {"perception":1} on this record, and passiveItemBonus() in src/rules/derive.ts (line 205, read at line 222) folds that into the Perception total for any worn/invested/equipped item with NO condition check. So the sight-only bonus is currently added to hearing and scent Perception checks too. The note claims only that the bonus 'needs the lookup to read worn/invested items' — i.e. that it cannot display at all — which is the opposite of the truth: it is already displaying, as part of the printed number.
correction: Keep situational true, +1 item, target perception, condition 'to Perception checks that involve sight'. Replace the engineNote with: the +1 is already applied unconditionally via passiveEffects.perception; starring it without also gating or removing that passive would either double-advertise it or leave every non-visual Perception check inflated by 1. ItemPassiveEffects (src/rules/types.ts, ~line 842) has no predicate/condition field at all, so this needs a real engine change (a conditional item-passive lane), not just extending the lookup past feats. Set needsEngineWork true.

problem: Same as the base goggles. passiveEffects is {"perception":2} in core.json, applied flat by passiveItemBonus() to every Perception check regardless of sense, so the sight-only restriction is currently ignored by the maths. The engineNote asserts the bonus cannot be shown until the lookup reads items, when it is in fact already inside the printed Perception modifier.
correction: Keep situational true, +2 item, perception, sight-only. Correct the engineNote as for obsidian-goggles: the +2 is already unconditionally in the total via passiveEffects.perception, ItemPassiveEffects has no predicate field, and needsEngineWork should be true.

problem: Same as the base goggles. passiveEffects is {"perception":3}, folded flat into all Perception checks by passiveItemBonus(); the engineNote's claim that the bonus cannot display without a lookup change is false and it omits that non-visual Perception is currently over-counted by 3.

problem: The situational:true call is right (Foundry predicate {or: acting, orating, performing-comedy, singing}), but the engineNote is wrong in the same load-bearing way as the goggles: core.json already carries passiveEffects {"skills":{"performance":1}}, which passiveItemBonus() adds to Performance unconditionally. Replace the engineNote: the +1 is already unconditionally in the Performance total via passiveEffects.skills.performance, so this record needs the passive gated or removed at the same time as the star is added; ItemPassiveEffects has no predicate field, so needsEngineWork is true, not false.

problem: Same as the base mask. passiveEffects is {"skills":{"performance":2}} and is applied flat to every Performance check, so the four-type restriction is not honoured by the maths. The engineNote claims the bonus merely 'needs the lookup to read worn/invested items'.
correction: Keep situational true, +2 item, skill/performance, same four-type restriction. Correct the engineNote as for persona-mask and set needsEngineWork true. (The fortune reroll is correctly excluded — its trigger, 'You fail a Performance check that benefits from the mask's bonus', confirms the bonus is the restricted one.)

problem: The reasonIfNot misquotes the record. It says the Spiritual Light activation 'imposes a -1 status penalty on OTHER creatures' Deception and Stealth checks — that is a penalty on enemies'. The record says: 'Creatures in the light receive a –1 status penalty to Deception and Stealth checks.' There is no 'other' and no 'enemies' in that clause; the wearer, standing inside their own light, is a creature in the light. The greater and major versions prove the wording is deliberate — the same sentence says 'Creatures in the light receive a –N status penalty' but 'your enemies in the light gain weakness N to spirit damage'. The spec's broadening is used to dismiss the effect entirely, and it also asserts 'the app has no target-side modifier surface for it' as the reason to drop it, which does not apply to a self-penalty.
correction: The +1 item bonus to Religion is correctly unconditional (Foundry: unpredicated FlatModifier on 'religion'; core.json passiveEffects {"skills":{"religion":1}}) — that part stands. But the dismissal of the activation is unsound: RAW the wearer takes a –1 status penalty to Deception and Stealth for the 10 minutes their own Spiritual Light is active. The registry already carries self-penalties in exactly this shape (barbarian-dedication: targets [{kind:'ac'}], when 'while raging', bonus '-1 (penalty)' at src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:69), so it is in scope. Set needsHumanDecision true with the question: should a self-inflicted penalty from your own once-per-day activated light be starred on Deception and Stealth, or treated as a Mode? Do not assert it lands only on enemies. Side note for the app owner: this record's light radius is missing in core.json ('The symbol casts dim light in a .'); Foundry's TokenLight gives dim 20 ft.

problem: Same misquote as the base item. The reasonIfNot says 'The activation's -2 status penalty to Deception/Stealth and weakness 5 to spirit damage land on creatures in the light, not on you' — but the record distinguishes the two halves explicitly: 'Creatures in the light receive a –2 status penalty to Deception and Stealth checks, and while it's active your enemies in the light gain weakness 5 to spirit damage.' Only the weakness is limited to enemies; the penalty is not, so 'not on you' is not supported by the text.
correction: The +2 item bonus to Religion is correctly unconditional and belongs in the Religion total. Correct the reasonIfNot to reflect that the –2 status penalty to Deception and Stealth applies to all creatures in the light, including the wearer, and set needsHumanDecision true with the same question as shining-symbol (star the self-penalty vs. model it as a Mode).

problem: Same misquote as the base item. The reasonIfNot claims the activation 'affects other creatures in the light (-3 status to Deception/Stealth, weakness 10 to spirit), not your own stats', but the record reads 'Creatures in the light receive a –3 status penalty to Deception and Stealth checks, and while it's active your enemies in the light gain weakness 10 to spirit damage' — the enemy restriction attaches only to the weakness.
correction: The +3 item bonus to Religion is correctly unconditional. Correct the reasonIfNot to reflect that the –3 status penalty to Deception and Stealth applies to all creatures in the light, the wearer included, and set needsHumanDecision true with the same question as shining-symbol.

problem: The two bonus entries are correct, but the engineNote is factually wrong about the record's text and would produce a real over-buff if acted on. It says: "The '+4 major striking holy' runes, void resistance 10, Unfettered Movement and the doomed suppression are unconditional-while-wielding effects and belong in the maths / effects". The record reads: "While wielding Serithtial, AGAINST EFFECTS CREATED BY FOLLOWERS OF ZON-KUTHON you gain the benefit of Unfettered Movement, a +4 status bonus to saves against death and void effects, void resistance 10, and suppress the doomed condition." The 'against effects created by followers of Zon-Kuthon' clause governs the whole list, not just the +4. Only the +4 major striking holy runes are genuinely unconditional.
correction: Keep both authored bonuses as-is (strikeDamage +2d6 vs Zon-Kuthon worshippers; save/all +4 status vs death and void effects created by followers of Zon-Kuthon). Rewrite the engineNote: only the '+4 major striking holy' runes (and the cold-iron/silver material treatment) are unconditional while wielding and belong in the maths. Unfettered Movement, void resistance 10 and the doomed suppression are ALL conditional on the effect having been created by a follower of Zon-Kuthon — they must NOT be folded into the character's permanent effects/resistances (a permanent void resistance 10 and permanent freedom-of-movement at level 23 would be a significant, wrong buff). They carry no typed bonus so they still get no registry entry, but the note must not instruct the engine to apply them flat.

problem: needsEngineWork is set false (implicitly — the field is omitted) on the grounds that the +4 status to AC/saves is 'unusable by the wearer by definition, so I did not flag it as engine work'. That is inconsistent with how the identical gap was handled elsewhere in this same chunk: whip-tongue-sling (allies within 25 feet gain +1 status vs fear) and hippogriff-feather (bonus to a spell-conjured hand) were both flagged needsEngineWork true for exactly the same missing capability — a bonus a character grants to something other than themselves. Petrifying the activator changes who benefits, not whether the app can represent the grant.
correction: Set needsEngineWork true with the same engine note used for whip-tongue-sling: no target kind exists for a bonus conferred on OTHER creatures' AC/saves (party-buff target). Separately, the reasonIfNot's claim that the +1 to the armour's item bonus to AC 'belongs in the maths' is correct as a classification but is not currently true of the data — this record's passiveEffects contains only fire resistance 40, so the light/medium +1 AC is modelled nowhere. Worth calling out so it is not lost: it is an unconditional-maths gap, not a star.

problem: The classification (+1 circumstance to AC and to saves vs the corresponding damage type, situational, no hard-coded damage type) is correct, but the engineNote's factual claim about core.json is not: "core.json's copy of the damage table is mangled by the AoN scrape (tradition/damage pairs run together: arcane→force, divine→spirit, occult→mental, primal→poison)". The table in the record is newline-separated but the pairs are intact and read correctly (Arcane/Force, Divine/Spirit, Occult/Mental, Primal/Poison) — nothing is run together or lost.

The correct reason for not hard-coding a damage type is the rules reason the spec also gives: the type depends on which dragon the hide came from, and the app has nowhere to record that choice, so the condition text must defer to the player. Same note is inherited by dragonhide-armor-standard-grade and dragonhide-armor-high-grade, whose descriptions are byte-identical blobs of the same base-material text.

problem: Two defects, both in the Diplomacy half. (1) INVENTED CONDITION ON ANOTHER RECORD: the needsHumanDecision question states "Same pattern on Warleader's Bulwark." That is false. Warleader's Bulwark reads "You gain a +2 item bonus to Diplomacy checks, but you take a -2 item penalty to Stealth checks to Hide and Sneak and Deception checks to Impersonate" — there is NO creature-type exception anywhere in that record (nor in the Greater, which is identical at +3/-3). Holy Chain is the only 'unconditional-except-for-X' case in this chunk, so the question broadens a condition onto a record whose text does not have one. (2) DOUBLE-COUNT RISK: the +2 item Diplomacy is listed as a starred bonus while the same record carries passiveEffects.skills.diplomacy = 2 (verified in core.json), and the spec itself says so. Applied verbatim, the player sees a star reading '+2 item to Diplomacy against any creature that isn't a fiend' next to a Diplomacy total that already contains that +2 — reading it as an extra bonus inflates the check. The AC/saves half is correct and should stand.
correction: Keep the four entries derived from "You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saving throws against fiends." exactly as written (+1 circumstance to AC and to Fortitude/Reflex/Will vs fiends) — none of that is in passiveEffects, so the star is the only place it can surface. Remove the +2 item Diplomacy entry from `bonuses`, or rewrite it as a caveat rather than a bonus, e.g. when: 'the +2 item bonus already in your Diplomacy total does NOT apply against fiends' (a subtraction, not an addition). Reword the question to name Holy Chain only: 'This record's +2 item Diplomacy is already in the maths but the text excludes fiends — should unconditional-except-for-X bonuses also be starred as a caveat, or only bonuses absent from the total?' Drop the Warleader's Bulwark sentence; those two records' Diplomacy bonuses are flatly unconditional and are correctly excluded from their own specs.

problem: The bonus itself is right ("You gain a +5 foot status bonus to your Speed for 1 minute"), but needsEngineWork is FALSE and it targets kind 'speed' — which the app does not support anywhere. targetMatches() in C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\situationalBonuses.ts (line ~373) only has cases for skill/save/perception/ac/attack and returns false in `default`, so a 'speed' target can never match. explainStat's `case 'speed'` (C:\trying ai 2\pf2e codex\src\rules\explain.ts line 562-611) is the only breakdown that never builds a `situational` array, and Speed is not among the starred defense tiles in VitalsRail.tsx. The entry would be silently dead data.

problem: Same defect: '+10 foot status bonus to your Speed for 1 hour' is correct, but needsEngineWork:false is wrong for the unsupported 'speed' target kind.

problem: The Lore line uses `skill: 'lore'`, which is not a valid key. problem: The 5th entry puts the Escape bonus on targetKind 'strikeAttack', and justifies it by claiming this "matches existing entries such as 'musetouched' and 'amorphous-aspect' which list acrobatics + athletics". That justification is false: both of those entries in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts contain ONLY acrobatics + athletics and no attack target at all (line 218: "musetouched": targets acrobatics, athletics, when "to Escape"; line 53: "amorphous-aspect": targets acrobatics, athletics, when "to Escape or Squeeze"). 'strikeAttack' in the allowed list means Strike attack rolls, and this bonus never applies to a Strike - it applies to an Escape check that happens to use the unarmed attack modifier, so it would star the character's attack line for a bonus that never touches an attack. The spec is also internally inconsistent: it adds the unarmed-option entry for the always-on +1 but not for the +4 circumstance Miraculous Escape bonus, which is the same check and has the same three roll options.
