If the app owner instead wants the unarmed-attack option represented, it must be added to BOTH the +1 item and the +4 circumstance bonuses, and it belongs on a new Escape/unarmed target kind rather than 'strikeAttack' - flag that as needsEngineWork/needsHumanDecision rather than reusing strikeAttack. Verified text: "While wearing a miniaturization module, you gain a +1 item bonus to checks to Escape" and Miraculous Escape "attempt to Escape the triggering effect, gaining a +4 circumstance bonus to this check".

problem: The engineNote broadens a condition beyond the text: it states "The aura is 'suppressed when you aren't holding the banner or wielding the weapon it is affixed to', which is a further gate the app cannot detect." In the record the suppression sentence belongs to the LIGHT effect and is quoted out of position - the base paragraph reads "This magical banner exudes bright light in the banner's aura (and dim light in an area equal to twice the banner's aura). This effect is suppressed when you aren't holding the banner or wielding the weapon it is affixed to." "This effect" refers to the light. The Major tier's save bonus is a separate, later sentence ("This magical banner also grants a +1 status bonus to saving throws against unholy effects to all creatures within the banner's aura") and the text never says the save bonus is suppressed.
correction: Rewrite the engineNote to say the suppression clause applies to the banner's LIGHT effect, not demonstrably to the unholy-save bonus; the only stated gate on the save bonus is being within the banner's aura. Everything else in this spec is right and should stand: situational true, +1 status, targetKind save, save 'all' (text says "saving throws", unqualified), and the warning that only the MAJOR tier grants it - the base 'dawnfire-beacon' record I read is light-only and must get no save entry.

problem: The engineNote calls Battering Blow "reaction-triggered". The record shows it is a FREE action with a trigger, not a reaction: the description reads "**Activate-Battering Blow** ⟨4⟩" (glyph 4 = free action) and the record's own field is "activationCost": { "type": "free" }. The record also has no frequency/counters entry for it, so the note's framing as a limited reaction is doubly off.
correction: Change "reaction-triggered" to "free action with a trigger (your melee Strike reduces an enemy's shield below its Broken Threshold), no frequency limit". The bonus itself is correct and should stand unchanged: +2 circumstance, targetKind skill/athletics, applying only to the Battering Blow Trip check and only in the sub-case "If your attack was powerful enough to destroy the shield outright".

problem: Marked situational:false with needsEngineWork, on the claim that "none of the allowed target kinds fits" the DC it boosts. That analysis is wrong. The text is "A flickering weapon adds its item bonus from its potency rune to the DC against attempts to Disarm or Steal it." Per core.json's own action records, Disarm is "Attempt an Athletics check against the target's Reflex DC" and Steal's "DC is usually the Perception DC of the creature wearing the object" — i.e. the DCs being raised are the WIELDER'S Reflex DC and Perception DC, both of which are existing target kinds. The spec also claims the derived magnitude is unrepresentable, but the live registry already carries exactly this shape: disarming-intercept uses bonus "item bonus equal to your armor's potency rune".
correction: situational: true. Two entries on the weapon's id: {bonus: "item bonus equal to the weapon's potency rune", when: "to your Reflex DC against attempts to Disarm this weapon from you", target: {kind: 'save', save: 'reflex'}} and {bonus: "item bonus equal to the weapon's potency rune", when: "to your Perception DC against attempts to Steal this weapon", target: {kind: 'perception'}}. Drop needsEngineWork. Set needsHumanDecision instead, question: "This bonus lands on the DC side (your Reflex/Perception DC that an enemy rolls against), not on a roll you make. Every current registry entry marks a stat the player rolls. Should DC-side bonuses get a star on Reflex/Perception, or does that mislead?" The Dazzled-on-crit rider is correctly excluded.

problem: The classification (situational:false for the wearer; the conditional bonus goes to an ally) is correct, but the engineNote states a false reason: "(b) the bonus size is variable (equal to the wearer's cursebound condition value), which the fixed 'bonus' string cannot express." The registry's bonus field is a free string and already carries variable magnitudes — deathless-servant: "status bonus equal to your wounded value"; disarming-intercept: "item bonus equal to your armor's potency rune"; mutant-physique: "mutagen's item bonus"; necromantic-deflection: "shield's circumstance bonus". Leaving this in would send the app owner to build engine work that already exists.
correction: Keep situational:false and needsEngineWork:true, but reduce the engineNote to the one real gap: the bonus targets ANOTHER character's saving throw and there is no target kind for an ally's stat (the closest precedent, terrain-scout, records an ally effect as bonus: "ally benefit (no roll bonus)" on the wearer's own stat). Delete the variable-magnitude claim — "status bonus equal to your cursebound value" is already an expressible bonus string.

problem: Same false engineNote as the base veil: "a variable magnitude tied to the wearer's cursebound value" is presented as an engine gap. Variable-magnitude bonus strings are already supported and in use in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts.
correction: Keep situational:false and needsEngineWork:true; the only genuine gap is the ally-targeted save/attack roll (no target kind for another character's stat). Remove the variable-magnitude half of the note.

problem: MISSING BONUS (coverage), and inconsistent with sibling records. The spec authors only the Performance half and dismisses the Hand Chords activation in engineNote as 'a duration-limited activated buff, not authored here'. But the record's own text is self-inclusive: 'You and all allies within a gain a +1 status bonus to the next attack roll, Perception check, saving throw, or skill check you attempt before the end of your next turn.' That is exactly the same shape as fife-of-the-faithful's Call to Arms and warpipes' Inspirational Salute, both of which the SAME batch DID author as situational entries (and for fife it even raised the human-decision question 'this is exactly the Fort/Reflex says nothing case the user reported, so it may be wanted'). Deciding the identical rules question three different ways in one batch is a bug in its own right, and here it silently drops a bonus that reaches the wearer.
correction: Either author the Hand Chords buff on bellows-pipes the way fife/warpipes were authored — '+1 status', when: 'on your next attack roll, Perception check, saving throw or skill check before the end of your next turn, after you Activate Hand Chords (1/day); choose which roll before rolling' across targetKind save (save:'all'), perception, skill ('all') and strikeAttack, with needsEngineWork true (the printed 'attack roll' is broader than strikeAttack, and it also lands on allies) — or set needsHumanDecision true here with the same question fife-of-the-faithful asks, so one answer covers all three. Do not leave it silently unrepresented while its siblings are represented.

problem: CONDITION BROADENED BEYOND THE TEXT. The authored 'when' says the initiative bonus '...also applies to allies within 120 feet'. The record says: 'You and your allies within 120 feet can Hustle for 1 additional hour. If you enter an encounter during this time period, the effect ends, but you receive a +2 status bonus to your initiative rolls for that encounter.' The 120-foot ally clause governs the extra hour of Hustle only; the bonus sentence is 'you receive', singular and unqualified. Extending it to allies is an invention, and it goes straight into player-facing display text.
correction: Drop the ally clause from the 'when'. Use: '+2 status', when: 'on your initiative roll, if you enter an encounter during the extra hour of Hustle granted by Forward March! (Activate, 1/day)'. Keep needsEngineWork true for the missing initiative statistic (the perception mapping follows the existing ambush-awareness / all-this-has-happened-before convention and is fine), but move the ally question — whether the ally Hustle clause is meant to carry the initiative bonus too — into engineNote as an ambiguity rather than asserting it, or raise it as needsHumanDecision.

problem: WRONG TARGET, and needsHumanDecision is set to false on a call that is not the classifier's to make. The record grants ONLY a defence DC bonus: 'you gain a +1 item bonus to your Fortitude DC against forced movement effects and to your Reflex DC against effects that would knock you prone.' The wearer never gets a bonus to a Fortitude or Reflex saving throw they roll. Authoring it under targetKind 'save' puts a star on the Fortitude and Reflex rows — the two numbers the player rolls — for a bonus that applies to neither. The spec's own engineNote admits 'the display text must say DC, otherwise players will add it to a save they roll', which is a description of the bug, not a fix: the star is on the wrong statistic regardless of the caption. Contrast boots-of-the-dead, where the text grants saves AND DCs, so the save entry there is legitimately correct.
correction: Set needsHumanDecision true and ask the owner: 'Should a bonus to a defence DC (Fortitude DC vs Shove/Reposition, Reflex DC vs Trip) be shown as a star on the Fortitude/Reflex save rows, or does it need a separate defence-DC display?' Until that is answered, report bonuses: [] with needsEngineWork true and the note 'no target kind for Fortitude DC / Reflex DC (the number an opponent rolls against)'. If the owner does want it on the save rows, keep the two entries but the 'when' must lead with the word DC, e.g. 'to your Fortitude DC (not your Fortitude save) against forced movement effects — an enemy Shoving or Repositioning you'.

problem: The target is authored as skill "lore:*". That literal never matches anything: `targetMatches` in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:373 compares the detail by exact string equality — `return ref.kind === 'skill' && (t.detail === 'all' || t.detail === ref.skill)`. The only wildcard the engine understands is `all`; a character's lore ref carries a concrete key (e.g. `lore:warfare`). So this entry would be silently inert — the star would never appear on any Lore skill, which is exactly the coverage bug this pass exists to fix. (The classification itself is right: the record does say "granting you a +1 item bonus to your check using the chosen Lore skill", and it is conditional on adding the visual trait to Recall Knowledge to study the tattoos.)
correction: Author it as `targets: [{ kind: 'skill', detail: 'all' }]` with the condition text carrying the restriction — e.g. when: "to Recall Knowledge with the Lore skill you chose when the tattoo was applied, when you add the visual trait to study your tattoos", bonus: "+1 item". Keep needsEngineWork true for the real fix (a per-item Lore choice, or wildcard support for a `lore:*` detail in targetMatches).

problem: The spec sets situational:true but supplies no `bonuses` array at all, so the record classifies as situational while producing zero registry rows. A consumer keying off `situational` gets an entry it cannot author; a consumer keying off `bonuses` drops it entirely. The record's text is confirmed ("If you are a demon, it amplifies any auras you have by granting a +1 item bonus to your aura's DCs.") and the reasoning — no aura-DC target exists, classDc would be the wrong stat, and the app has no creature-type gate for the PC — is correct.
correction: Set situational:false with needsEngineWork:true and put the analysis in reasonIfNot/engineNote: "+1 item bonus to your auras' DCs, only if you are a demon — no representable target (aura DC is not classDc, and the app has no PC creature-type gate)." That keeps the record out of the registry without a true-but-empty row.

problem: The second entry hangs a DC-only bonus on kind 'perception' with bonus string "+2 item". The record says "+2 item bonus to Diplomacy checks to Make an Impression and to their Perception DC when someone attempts to Lie to them" — the bonus is to the DC an opponent rolls against, never to the wearer's own Perception check. The sheet renders the `bonus` field verbatim next to the stat, so a player opening Perception reads "+2 item" and can reasonably add it to a Perception roll. Burying the correction in the `when` prose does not undo the misleading number. (The first entry, +2 item to Diplomacy to Make an Impression, is correct.)
correction: Move the qualifier into the `bonus` field so the rendered number can't be misread — e.g. bonus: "+2 item to your Perception DC (not to your Perception check)", when: "when someone attempts to Lie to you". Keep needsEngineWork true until a Perception-DC target exists; if the owner prefers, suppress the entry entirely rather than show a non-additive number on the Perception line.

problem: The DATA call (situational:false) is right, but the engineNote makes a false factual claim about the app: "this weapon's attack modifier is currently 2 too low when thrown". Alchemical bombs are not weapons in core.json at all — `d.items['greater-defoliation-bomb']` (and every one of the 254 bomb-trait items, e.g. moderate-nail-bomb, alchemist's-fire, bottled-lightning) is `itemType: "equipment"` with no `category`, `group`, `damage` or `hands` field, unlike `longsword` which has `itemType: "weapon", category: "martial", group: "sword", damage: {dice:1,die:"d8",type:"slashing"}`. There is no Strike for the app to be "2 too low" on. The same understated note is repeated on the other 15 graded-bomb specs (major-defoliation-bomb, moderate/greater/major nail-bomb, moderate/greater/major inflammation-flask, moderate/greater/major spider-satchel, moderate/greater/major durian-bomb, moderate/greater/major tenderizer-grenade), all phrased as if a bomb Strike existed and only the item bonus were missing.
correction: Keep situational:false and needsEngineWork:true, but restate the note: bombs are not modeled as weapons (itemType 'equipment', no damage/category/group), so they produce no Strike at all; the engine work needed is bomb-as-thrown-weapon support (damage dice, splash, bomb proficiency) with the grade's item bonus to attack rolls fed into that Strike's item slot — derive.ts's `potencyBonus` (line 1188: `Math.max(abpOn(c) ? abpAttack(c.level) : runes?.potency ?? 0, mpRef?.attack ?? 0)`) reads runes/ABP/Monster-Parts only and would need a third source. Verified correct in these specs: the quoted grade texts, the +1/+2/+3 progression, and that the lesser grade of every family grants no attack bonus.

problem: Inconsistent treatment of activation-gated Strike-damage riders inside the same batch, asserted at confidence 'high' with needsHumanDecision:false on both sides. clay-sphere/greater-clay-sphere/major-clay-sphere each list a strikeDamage entry for "Until the end of your next turn, Strikes with the affixed weapon have their damage dice increase by one step" — which is itself gated behind "After you cast a morph or polymorph spell by activating the clay sphere". cleft-head-marking/lesser-cleft-head-marking/greater-cleft-head-marking drop the structurally identical "Activate—Unexpected Strike (concentrate) Frequency once per day; Trigger You Strike a creature that has the off-guard condition with a weapon attack; Effect You deal an extra 1d6 precision damage" (2d6 at greater) as "a triggered rider, not a stat bonus". Both are Activate-gated, time/frequency-limited, and modify the character's own Strike damage; one is starred and the other is not.
correction: Pick one rule and apply it to both. Either (a) add a strikeDamage entry to all three cleft-head records — bonus: '1d6 precision damage' (2d6 for greater-cleft-head-marking), when: 'once per day, when you Activate Unexpected Strike after Striking an off-guard creature with a weapon (tattoo must be invested)' — or (b) drop the strikeDamage entry from the three clay-sphere records too, on the grounds that Activate effects are surfaced by the item's activation list rather than by a stat star. Set needsHumanDecision:true with that question for the app owner, since it decides whether every activation-granted damage rider in the collection gets a star. Everything else in these six specs is verified correct: +1 item to Deception to Feint (+2 at greater, "The item bonus is +2"), the invested trait is genuinely on all three tattoos, and clay sphere's save bonus is +1/+2/+3 item vs morph or polymorph while affixed to armor.

problem: The engineNote asserts "The base +3 item bonus from the major resilient rune is UNCONDITIONAL and belongs in the armour maths; only the extra +1 against poison is situational, so the star should read as 'a +4 instead of +3'". That claim is false for this record. The core.json entry for slithermaws-bane-artifact has NO usage field, no armor category, no runes and no save entries in passiveEffects (its passiveEffects contains only the poison resistance 15). The +3 major resilient bonus is therefore nowhere in the app's maths, so a star that reads "+4 instead of +3" points the player at a baseline number the sheet never shows. The bonus values themselves (+4 item vs poison, +2 circumstance after Adaptation) are correct and are correctly typed.
correction: Keep both bonus entries as specified, but fix the framing: the first entry should read as a plain "+4 item bonus to saving throws against poison" with an explanatory clause ("the major resilient rune's +3, raised by 1 against poison") rather than "+4 instead of +3", and the record should carry needsEngineWork: true noting that this artifact is not modelled as armour at all (no usage/armor/rune data), so the underlying resilient +3 is missing from every save total. Also, the second entry's duration is slightly under-stated: the text says the Adaptation effect lasts "until your next daily preparations or the next time you activate it, whichever comes first" — add the second clause.

problem: Condition broadened beyond the text. The engineNote says "Requires being the anointed ruler of Kyonin or having their permission — a fiction gate, not a roll condition", presented as governing the record. In the record's own description that clause is scoped to the apex paragraph only: "If you are the properly anointed ruler of Kyonin, or if that ruler has given you permission to wear the crown for a time, as long as you have the Viridian Crown invested, choose either Charisma or Wisdom." Both situational bonuses sit in later paragraphs gated only on investment — "As long as you have the crown invested, it imparts knowledge of the Fortifying Brew and Resurrect rituals. When you cast either of these ... you gain a +3 item bonus to your skill check", and the Elven Hope activation, which states no rulership requirement. The two bonus entries' own when strings are correct; only the note attaches a gate the text does not.
correction: Restrict the rulership gate to the apex attribute increase in the engineNote ("the Cha-or-Wis apex boost — and only that — requires being Kyonin's anointed ruler or having their permission"). Leave both bonus entries as written; they are correctly conditioned on investment / on Sustaining Elven Hope. Separately worth recording in the note: core.json hard-codes apexAttribute: "cha" although the item lets you choose Charisma or Wisdom and re-choose every 24 hours.

problem: The drawback "-1 penalty to attack rolls and save DCs of offensive spells" is filed ONLY under targetKind 'spell', and needsHumanDecision is set false. On the plain reading only the *save DCs* are qualified "of offensive spells"; the attack-roll penalty is unrestricted - corroborated by the very next clause, which penalises "all weapon, unarmed attack, and spell damage" (the spec itself files that one under strikeDamage). As specced, a martial character drinking a serene mutagen sees a -1 marker on nothing but spells while their Strikes silently keep the penalty.
correction: Add a row: bonus "-1 untyped", when "drawback - to all attack rolls (weapon, unarmed and spell) while a serene mutagen is active", targetKind "strikeAttack"; keep the existing 'spell' row but narrow its `when` to "to the save DCs of offensive spells". If the app owner prefers the narrow spell-only reading, set needsHumanDecision true with the question "does 'a -1 penalty to attack rolls and save DCs of offensive spells' restrict the attack-roll penalty to spell attacks, or to all attack rolls?" rather than resolving it silently.

problem: Same as the parent record: the -1 attack-roll penalty is filed only under 'spell'. Record text: "**Drawback** You take a -1 penalty to attack rolls and save DCs of offensive spells, and a -1 penalty per damage die to all weapon, unarmed attack, and spell damage." Weapon/unarmed Strikes get no marker even though the damage half of the same sentence explicitly covers them.
correction: Add "-1 untyped" / when "drawback - to all attack rolls while the lesser serene mutagen is active" / targetKind "strikeAttack"; restrict the existing 'spell' row's `when` to "to the save DCs of offensive spells". Otherwise set needsHumanDecision true with the scope question.

problem: Same defect: "-1 penalty to attack rolls and save DCs of offensive spells" recorded only as targetKind 'spell', so no attack-roll marker exists for a weapon user.
correction: Add "-1 untyped" / when "drawback - to all attack rolls while the moderate serene mutagen is active" / targetKind "strikeAttack"; narrow the 'spell' row to the save DCs of offensive spells, or flag needsHumanDecision.

problem: Same defect: the attack-roll half of the drawback is dropped into the 'spell' row only.
correction: Add "-1 untyped" / when "drawback - to all attack rolls while the greater serene mutagen is active" / targetKind "strikeAttack"; narrow the 'spell' row to the save DCs of offensive spells, or flag needsHumanDecision.

problem: Same defect: the attack-roll half of the drawback is dropped into the 'spell' row only.
correction: Add "-1 untyped" / when "drawback - to all attack rolls while the major serene mutagen is active" / targetKind "strikeAttack"; narrow the 'spell' row to the save DCs of offensive spells, or flag needsHumanDecision.

problem: The second bonus is attached to targetKind 'perception'. The record's own text is: "you gain a +1 item bonus to Diplomacy checks and to your Perception DC for 10 minutes". A Perception DC is the number OTHERS roll against — it is never added to any Perception check you make. Putting it on the perception target makes the sheet star Perception and tell the player they have a bonus on a roll that in fact gets nothing. That is the exact 'misleading marker' failure the brief warns about, and needsEngineWork alone does not neutralise it because the marker still renders on the wrong stat.
correction: Keep only the Diplomacy entry: { bonus: '+1 item', when: 'for 10 minutes after you drink it (1 hour if brewed with the Tea Ceremony), to Diplomacy checks', target: { kind: 'skill', skill: 'diplomacy' } }. Drop the perception entry from the registry and record the Perception-DC clause as needsEngineWork prose only (the app has no Perception DC stat), or set needsHumanDecision asking the owner whether a Perception DC display should be added. Everything else in this spec (situational true, +1 item, durations 10 minutes / 1 hour with the Tea Ceremony) is confirmed correct.

problem: Low severity, but unflagged: the condition 'while in mountainous terrain' is stated as an ONGOING requirement with confidence 'high'. The record's text reads "For the listed duration, drinking this elixir while in mountainous terrain protects you from the effects of severe cold and grants you an item bonus to Athletics checks made to Climb, High Jump, or Long Jump" — grammatically the terrain qualifies the act of DRINKING, not the whole duration. Under the printed wording, drinking it in the Kodars and then descending arguably keeps the bonus; under the spec's wording it is lost. The same sentence (and the same spec wording) appears verbatim in moderate-elixir-of-the-peaks, greater-elixir-of-the-peaks and major-elixir-of-the-peaks, so the same correction applies to all four.
correction: Either phrase the condition to mirror the text — when: 'for 1 hour after drinking it in mountainous terrain, to Athletics checks to Climb, High Jump, or Long Jump' — or keep the current wording but drop confidence to medium and set needsHumanDecision: 'Does the mountainous-terrain clause gate only the moment of drinking, or the whole duration?'. Everything else in the four elixir specs is confirmed against the record: +1/1 hour (lesser), +2/one day (moderate), +3/1 day (greater), +3/7 days (major), item type, Athletics target, and the high-altitude save clause with no printed save type.

problem: Emits ten separate skill entries (athletics, performance, skill:'all' for Recall Knowledge, stealth, intimidation, diplomacy, medicine, survival, society, deception) for a record where the printed text grants exactly ONE of them: 'granting a +1 status bonus to skill checks determined by the relic's emotion'. Since core.json carries no effectChoices for the relic's emotion (I confirmed the record has none), the registry would put a star on ten skills at once for any character with this gift — the exact 'misleads the player' failure the marker is supposed to avoid. It is also internally inconsistent with how the same engineer handled the identical unknown-choice problem two records earlier: stone-of-unrivaled-skill ('the skill you chose for your contract') got ONE skill:'all' entry with the constraint in the condition text.
correction: Replace the ten entries with a single entry: bonus '+1 status', targetKind 'skill', skill 'all', when 'for 1 minute after activating the relic (once per hour), to checks with the one skill set by the relic's emotion — Anger Athletics, Awe Performance, Dedication Recall Knowledge, Fear Stealth, Hatred Intimidation, Joy Diplomacy, Love Medicine, Misery Survival, Pride Society, Remorse Deception'. Keep needsEngineWork true with the same note (an effectChoices block keyed on the relic's emotion would collapse this to one accurate marker). Bonus size, type (status) and duration in the spec are all correct.

problem: needsEngineWork is set to true, but nothing here is missing from the engine: the target is 'ac', which is in the supported list, and the reason given ('the condition is a creature type, which the app cannot evaluate') is the normal case for this display-only registry, not a gap. The same engineer marked needsEngineWork false for identical creature-type conditions in the same batch (token-of-salt-and-earth 'from creatures with the unholy trait', conrasu-coin-arbiter '+3 on a creature with the aeon trait', scrap-shot 'if the target is wearing metal armor'). The secondary reason offered — that relic gifts may not be attachable to a character — applies equally to scrap-shot, feather-steps, wind-barrier and enhancing-circuitry, all of which the same batch marked needsEngineWork false, so it cannot justify a different flag here.
correction: Set needsEngineWork false and drop the creature-type sentence from the engineNote. Keep the bonus entry exactly as written (+1 status, targetKind 'ac', 'to AC against attacks made by dragons') — that part matches the text verbatim. If the relic-gift reachability question is worth raising, raise it once as a batch-level note covering all eight relic-gift records (draconic-resistance, cleanse-soul, muse, emotion-surge, work-harden, enhancing-circuitry, scrap-shot, feather-steps, wind-barrier, track-of-the-beast), not on this one record. Worth adding to the note instead: this record is edition 'legacy-era', so the edition toggle may hide it regardless.

problem: The spec says only the Stealth penalty belongs in the maths and treats the sight-only Perception bonus as a clean situational entry with needsEngineWork:false. The record ALREADY has passiveEffects: { skills: { stealth: -1 }, perception: 1 }, and derive.ts:256 folds that perception:1 into the Perception total via passiveItemBonus(). So the app currently applies a sight-ONLY bonus to every Perception check (hearing, scent, Seek by smell), and adding a star on top would double-report the same +1.
correction: Keep the situational entry (+1 item, 'to Perception checks based on sight', kind perception) but set needsEngineWork:true with the note: remove (or gate) passiveEffects.perception on the shining-hackle record, because it currently over-applies the sight-restricted bonus to all Perception. The passiveEffects.skills.stealth = -1 is correct and must stay.

problem: engineNote/needsEngineWork:true claims the app 'needs the worn/invested item lane to feed a flat +1 item bonus into Society and into the Warfare Lore skill' and that 'the maths side must support per-Lore item bonuses'. Both are already done: the record carries passiveEffects: { skills: { society: 1, 'lore:warfare': 1 } }, and passiveItemBonus() (src/rules/derive.ts:205, used by the skill total at :273) reads per-skill and lore: keys directly.
correction: situational:false is right; set needsEngineWork:false and drop the engineNote — the unconditional +1 to Society and Warfare Lore is already wired and working.

problem: engineNote claims 'Needs the worn/invested item lane to add a flat +1 item bonus to Athletics'. The record already has passiveEffects: { skills: { athletics: 1 } } and the lane already consumes it.
correction: situational:false is right; set needsEngineWork:false and drop the engineNote.

problem: engineNote claims the worn/invested item lane is needed for the flat +2 to Athletics. The record already has passiveEffects: { skills: { athletics: 2 } } (correctly the greater value replacing, not stacking with, the base +1).
correction: situational:false is right; set needsEngineWork:false and drop the engineNote. The 10-foot swim Speed observation is fine.

problem: engineNote claims 'Needs the worn/invested item lane for the flat +1 item bonus to Acrobatics'. The record already has passiveEffects: { skills: { acrobatics: 1 } }.
correction: situational:false is right; set needsEngineWork:false and drop the engineNote.

problem: engineNote is half stale: it asks for 'the worn/invested item lane for the flat +1 item bonus to Stealth', but the record already has passiveEffects: { skills: { stealth: 1 } } and the lane already applies it.
correction: situational:false is right. Keep needsEngineWork:true but narrow the note to the ONLY real gap: while the Umbral Double activation is up the record's existing +1 Stealth must be suppressed, which wants a Mode/toggle, not a situational star. Drop the 'needs the item lane' half.

problem: engineNote point (1) says the base +1 item bonus to Deception 'must go into the Deception total via the worn/invested item lane' as if that were outstanding work. The record already has passiveEffects: { skills: { deception: 1 } } and it is already in the total.
correction: Keep the single registered bonus (the +4 to the Deception DC during Monstrosity Meld) and keep needsEngineWork:true, but restrict the engineNote to the real gap — the registry has no DC-side target kind. Delete the claim that the base +1 still needs wiring.

problem: The Green entry uses skill: 'lore:*'. targetMatches() in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts:373-388 matches a skill target only when detail === 'all' or detail === the exact skill key (e.g. 'lore:warfare'). No entry in the existing 308-row registry uses any lore key at all. 'lore:*' is not a supported wildcard, so that entry would silently match nothing and never render a star — a dead row rather than a visible bug.
correction: Either use skill:'all' with the restriction carried in the 'when' text ('Green paradigm active: to Lore checks to Recall Knowledge while in the area (1 minute)'), or set needsEngineWork:true asking for wildcard/prefix handling in targetMatches for 'lore:*'. The other five colours are verbatim-correct (Red=Intimidation to Coerce, Yellow=Intimidation to Demoralize, Orange=Performance, Blue=Perception to Sense Motive, Indigo=Stealth to Hide), and the ally-aura / mutually-exclusive concerns are valid.

problem: The needsHumanDecision question says the concrete tiers are 'not in this chunk', implying they cannot be registered. They exist in core.json — twice: elixir-of-the-peaks-lesser / -moderate / -greater / -major carry clean per-tier text ('grants you a +1 item bonus to Athletics checks made to Climb, High Jump, or Long Jump'), while lesser-/moderate-/greater-/major-elixir-of-the-peaks duplicate the whole container blob.
correction: Keep situational:true and the two targets (skill/athletics for Climb/High Jump/Long Jump, save/all vs high altitude). Rephrase the question to name the real ids and note the duplicate-id pair, so the owner can choose the elixir-of-the-peaks-<tier> records (clean text, +1/+2/+3/+3 with 1 hour / 1 day / 1 day / 7 days) and skip the container.

problem: The second entry maps the Do No Harm penalty to targetKind 'strikeDamage', but the text reads 'Both you and the triggering enemy take a -4 status penalty to damage rolls until the end of your next turn' — ALL damage rolls, including spell damage, not only Strike damage. needsEngineWork:false is therefore wrong: no listed target kind expresses 'any damage roll', and the current SituationalTarget type has no damage kind at all (only skill/save/perception/ac/attack).
correction: The +1 item to Diplomacy entry is verbatim-correct — keep it. For the penalty, set needsEngineWork:true and reword the 'when' to 'to ALL your damage rolls (Strikes and spells alike) until the end of your next turn'; note that 'strikeDamage' under-scopes it. The needsHumanDecision question about whether penalties belong in this registry is a fair one to keep.

problem: Same target-scoping error as the base armband: the -8 status penalty is to damage rolls generally ('the status penalty to damage rolls from Do No Harm increases to -8'), not specifically Strike damage, and needsEngineWork is set to false.
correction: Both skill entries are correct as written (+2 item to Medicine limited to Administer First Aid / Treat Wounds, and the carried-forward +1 item to Diplomacy — the record does embed the base text, so carrying it forward is right). For the -8 entry set needsEngineWork:true and reword to 'to ALL your damage rolls (Strikes and spells alike)'.

problem: WRONG TARGET. The record says "You and allies within the banner's aura gain a +2 item bonus to Perception DCs" — a bonus to the Perception DC (the number a creature Sneaking/Hiding rolls against), NOT to Perception checks. The spec's engineNote diagnoses this correctly but then emits a bonus with targetKind 'perception' anyway. Any consumer that reads `bonuses` and ignores the prose will star the character's Perception and a player will add +2 to Perception ROLLS near the banner — the exact inflation the brief warns about.
correction: Emit NO bonus entry. Keep situational true, bonuses empty, needsEngineWork true with the note: 'bonus is to the Perception DC; the sheet has no Perception-DC stat (SituationalTarget kinds are skill/save/perception/ac/attack, and `perception` means Perception checks). Also a deployed party aura, so it is positional and covers allies.' Do not use targetKind 'perception' for a DC.

problem: WRONG TARGET, same defect at +3. Record text: "You and allies within the banner's aura gain a +3 item bonus to Perception DCs and protection from severe cold and heat." Emitting targetKind 'perception' turns a defence number into a bonus on the player's Perception checks.
correction: Emit NO bonus entry; situational true with bonuses empty and needsEngineWork true ('+3 item to Perception DC — no Perception-DC stat exists; aura/positional and party-wide'). Handle identically to the greater version.

problem: WRONG TARGET, twice over. Record: "An animal companion wearing anti-dragon barding gains a +4 item bonus to its Fortitude DC and Reflex DC against attempts to grapple, reposition, shove, or trip it." (1) These are DCs an attacker's Athletics check is rolled against, not saving throws; (2) they belong to the ANIMAL COMPANION, not the character. The spec nevertheless emits two entries with targetKind 'save' (fortitude and reflex), which would put a star on the PLAYER's Fortitude and Reflex saves reading '+4 item vs attempts to Grapple/Reposition/Shove/Trip' — a bonus the player does not have on a roll they do not make.
correction: Emit NO bonus entries. situational true, bonuses empty, needsEngineWork true: 'targets the animal companion's Fortitude DC and Reflex DC — the registry has neither a save-DC stat nor a companion-stat target; do not map a DC onto save/fortitude or save/reflex.' The 3d4 damage to a successful Grappler is correctly excluded.

problem: CONDITION WRONG / GARBLED. The record's gate is "Three Items (one 17th-level or higher item): If dominant emotion or emotion conduit counteract an effect, the target regains 5d10+5 Hit Points and gains a +2 status bonus to saving throws against mental effects for 10 minutes." The spec's player-facing `when` reads "...(requires three set items, one of 13th... in fact one of 17th level or higher)" — it states the wrong threshold, then self-corrects inside the string. 13th level belongs to different features (the Emotion Conduit gift and the recovery-check collective feature), so the text as written both misinforms and is unreadable at the table.
correction: when: 'for 10 minutes after dominant emotion or emotion conduit counteracts an effect — while you bear three or more Monk's Attire items, one of them 17th level or higher'. Bonus (+2 status), targetKind save with save 'all', and the caveat that "the target" may be an ally rather than the wearer are all correct as filed.

problem: CONDITIONAL BONUS MARKED UNCONDITIONAL. The record says "When played as an instrument, the busine ... grants a +2 item bonus to Performance checks" — an explicit usage gate. The spec sets situational false because passiveEffects.skills.performance = 2 already folds it into the maths (I confirmed that field). That means a bard doing an oratory, dance or singing Performance without the trumpet in hand still gets +2: a conditional bonus inflating every roll. The spec's own reasonIfNot concedes this, and it marked Battle Lute — identical wording — situational, so the chunk is internally inconsistent.
correction: Mark situational true: bonus '+2 item', when 'on Performance checks made while playing the busine as an instrument', targetKind 'skill', skill 'performance' — and flag that passiveEffects.skills.performance must be removed if the star is added, so the +2 is not counted twice. Keep the needsHumanDecision question, but note that whichever rule the owner picks must be applied to Busine and Battle Lute together (and to every other instrument item with this wording).

problem: The bonus itself is correct (+1 circumstance to Survival to Subsist), but the engineNote makes a factual claim about core.json that is false: "Trained Survival and the Forager feat are unconditional grants already covered by effectChoices." The record's only effectChoices entry is the trained-skill picker (prompt: "Choose a skill to become trained in (Survival by default...)"); the record has NO feat-grant field of any kind (keys are id,name,ancestryId,versatile,traits,rarity,description,descRefs,source,edition,effectChoices). An implementer reading that note would assume Forager is already handled when it is not.
correction: Keep the bonus entry unchanged. Reword the engineNote to: "Trained Survival is unconditional and already handled by the record's effectChoices. The Forager skill feat ('You gain the Forager skill feat as a bonus feat') is an unconditional grant that is NOT modelled anywhere on this record — separate work, not a situational bonus."

problem: Condition wording broadened past the rules on the split entries. The text is "a +2 circumstance bonus on your Fortitude or Reflex DC against attempts to Grapple or Trip you" — i.e. whichever DC the maneuver actually targets. The spec repeats BOTH maneuvers on BOTH entries, so the Fortitude marker reads "to your Fortitude DC against attempts to Grapple or Trip you" — but Trip targets the Reflex DC, never the Fortitude DC (and Grapple targets Fortitude DC, never Reflex). A player reading the Fortitude star is told something the rules do not grant. (Bonus size, type, targets and the Acrobatics/Balance entry are all correct.)
correction: Split the maneuvers to match which DC each targets: Fortitude entry when = "to your Fortitude DC against attempts to Grapple you, and to Fortitude saves against effects that would Grab you, Restrain you, or knock you prone"; Reflex entry when = "to your Reflex DC against attempts to Trip you, and to Reflex saves against effects that would Grab you, Restrain you, or knock you prone". Leave the Acrobatics (Balance) entry as authored.

problem: Same broadening as strong-oak. Text: "a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude or Reflex DC against attempts to Grapple or Trip you." The spec's Fortitude entry claims the bonus applies to your Fortitude DC against Trip attempts, and the Reflex entry claims it applies to your Reflex DC against Grapple attempts; Grapple checks are made against Fortitude DC and Trip against Reflex DC, so each entry names one maneuver it cannot apply to. Everything else (situational, +2 circumstance, the save half, the grantedStrikes note about the tail) verified correct against the record.
correction: Fortitude entry when = "to your Fortitude DC against attempts to Grapple you, and to Fortitude saves against effects that would Grab you, Restrain you, or knock you prone"; Reflex entry when = "to your Reflex DC against attempts to Trip you, and to Reflex saves against effects that would Grab you, Restrain you, or knock you prone".

problem: Same broadening. Text: "a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude or Reflex DC against attempts to Reposition, Shove, or Trip you." Reposition and Shove are made against the Fortitude DC; Trip against the Reflex DC. The spec puts all three maneuvers on both the Fortitude and the Reflex entry, so each marker overstates its coverage. The +2 circumstance value, the save-bonus half ("This bonus also applies to saving throws against spells or effects that attempt to force you to move or knock you prone") and the forced-movement-halving engineNote are all correct.
correction: Fortitude entry when = "to your Fortitude DC against attempts to Reposition or Shove you, and to Fortitude saves against effects that would force you to move or knock you prone"; Reflex entry when = "to your Reflex DC against attempts to Trip you, and to Reflex saves against effects that would force you to move or knock you prone".

problem: The engineNote asserts an importer defect: "the record's activationCost is stored as 'free' although the description prints a reaction-style '⟨4⟩ envision' activation". That is false. In this app ⟨4⟩ IS the free-action glyph — src/sheet/widgets.tsx, ActionGlyph: case 'free' returns <Glyph char="4" title="Free action" /> and case 'reaction' returns char="5". So activationCost {type:'free'} matches the printed ⟨4⟩ exactly; there is nothing to raise with the importer, and the note would send someone chasing a non-bug (the same ⟨4⟩/free pairing appears on cleft-head-marking-* and fate-tempters-ring, and ⟨5⟩/reaction on the flowing-water tattoos, all consistent).
correction: Drop the engineNote's importer claim. The bonus classification itself is correct and should stand as authored: +1 item, targetKind 'perception', when = "on hearing-based Perception checks, for 10 minutes after you Activate the aids (free action, once per day; requires your hearing aids to be currently on)".

problem: The engineNote says "the aura's radius is not stated in this record (it is a property of the banner the beacon is attached to)". Both halves are wrong. The record's own first line is "The warm, caring light of the sun glows from the center of this magical banner" — the Dawnfire Beacon IS the banner; its usage is 'affixed-or-held-in-one-hand', i.e. affixed to a WEAPON or held, never attached to some other banner. And the radius is knowable: the Foundry record models it as an Aura rule element with radius 30 (the standard Battlecry! banner aura). The condition also drops a requirement the record does print: "This effect is suppressed when you aren't holding the banner or wielding the weapon it is affixed to."
correction: Keep the entry (+1 status, targetKind 'save', save 'all') and keep needsEngineWork true for the ally/aura gap only. Rewrite the condition to "against unholy effects, while you're holding the banner (or wielding the weapon it's affixed to) and within its 30-foot aura", and replace the engineNote's radius claim with: radius is 30 feet per the banner aura. Flag needsHumanDecision on one point the text leaves genuinely ambiguous: the suppression sentence grammatically attaches to the LIGHT paragraph, and Foundry's Aura carries no holding predicate — so whether the save bonus is also suppressed when the banner isn't held is the owner's call.

problem: The engineNote claims the activation's "-2 circumstance penalty to saves against disease and to recover from sickened" "falls on creatures caught in the emanation (enemies), not on you — do not author it as a penalty on the wielder". The record does not say that. Its text is "the target creature, as well as any creatures within a [emanation], must succeed at a save... While within the emanation, the creature takes a –2 circumstance penalty to saves against disease and to recover from the sickened condition" — any creature, with no ally/enemy carve-out. core.json has dropped the emanation size (the text reads "within a , must succeed"); the Foundry source gives @Template[emanation|distance:10], a 10-foot emanation centred on the creature you just stabbed — which a melee wielder of a 10-ft-thrown dagger is normally standing inside. The stated reason for omitting it is therefore invalid.
correction: Keep the +1 status save-vs-paralysis entry as authored. Either add a second entry — bonus "-2 circumstance (penalty)", targetKind 'save', save 'all', when "on saves against disease and to recover from sickened, while you're within 10 feet of a creature struck by the activated ghast stiletto (1 minute)" — matching how the earplugs and feather-of-unfounded-bravado specs already carry penalties, or omit it and say so honestly ("self-inflicted edge case, owner chose not to surface it"). Also note as a data defect that the emanation distance is missing from the core.json description.

problem: needsEngineWork is left false while the engineNote itself lists two things the app cannot represent: "it is a ONE-SHOT bonus consumed by the next qualifying check, and it also benefits every other creature inside the lodge (allies)". The ally-facing half is exactly the reason the spec-writer set needsEngineWork true on dawnfire-beacon-major, so the two records are flagged inconsistently — and the one-shot-consumption behaviour is a gap no other entry in this chunk has, since a starred stat would keep advertising a +3 that was already spent.
correction: Set needsEngineWork true. Bonus/target/condition as authored (+3 item, targetKind 'skill', skill 'all', "on the NEXT Recall Knowledge check about a creature with the dream trait within 24 hours, after spending 10 minutes studying the lodge's trophies"). Missing engine support: (a) one-shot bonuses that are consumed by the next qualifying check, and (b) bonuses that also apply to other party members' sheets.

problem: needsEngineWork is left false (absent) although the engineNote states the blocking gap outright: "The +4 status damage applies only to the specific weapon sheathed in the scabbard, which the app does not track per-weapon." The clay-sphere specs set needsEngineWork true for the same class of problem (a bonus that depends on which item the gear is attached to), so this record is flagged inconsistently and the gap would be lost when the flags are triaged.
correction: Set needsEngineWork true. The entry itself is right and should stand (+4 status, targetKind 'strikeDamage', "for 1 round after you draw that weapon from the commandant's scabbard (one melee weapon of 1 Bulk or lighter)"), as is the call to leave the +3 item Athletics and the apex Strength out of the registry — both are confirmed present as passiveEffects.skills.athletics = 3 and apexAttribute 'str'. Missing engine support: recording which single weapon is sheathed in the scabbard so the marker lands on that weapon's strike only.

problem: Marked situational:false. The record says "Your clockwork components allow you to react to danger with alacrity. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls." The spec's own reasoning ('unconditional within its scope') conflates 'no extra trigger' with 'unconditional relative to the stat it is filed under'. Filed as targetKind perception, situational:false reads as 'fold this into the maths' — which would add +2 to Perception permanently and inflate Seek, Sense Motive and the passive Perception DC, exactly the failure mode the brief warns about. The spec's own engineNote even says 'It must NOT be added to the Perception total', contradicting the flag.
correction: Set situational: true. Keep the single entry {targetKind:'perception', bonus:'+2 circumstance', when:'on initiative rolls (Perception, or whichever skill you roll initiative with)'} and keep needsEngineWork:true for the missing initiative stat. This matches the two established precedents already in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts line 49 ("all-this-has-happened-before": perception, 'on your initiative roll (once per day)') and line 52 ("ambush-awareness": perception, 'on Perception checks rolled for initiative'), both of which are situational entries.

problem: Emits a +1 status bonus to all saves that the background does not grant. The bonus comes from the 'Bickering' option inside the Family adjustment block, and that block's own opening line in the record is "You can add one of the following two adjustments to ANY background" — it is opt-in, it replaces the background's skill feat, and it is available to every background, not these four. The same boilerplate is byte-identical in folklore-enthusiast, northridge-scholar and outskirt-dweller (I diffed all four). Writing it into the registry under a background id would star Fortitude/Reflex/Will for every character who picked one of these four backgrounds, including the overwhelming majority who never took the Family adjustment — a permanent false positive. It also triggers on ANOTHER PC's critical failure, which nothing in the app can observe. The spec author identified all of this in the engineNote and then emitted the bonus anyway.
correction: For all four Willowshore backgrounds (close-ties, folklore-enthusiast, northridge-scholar, outskirt-dweller): set bonuses to an empty array, situational:false with reasonIfNot 'the background itself grants no typed bonus', and keep needsHumanDecision:true. Bickering's +1 status to saves (and Close-Knit's DC-5 reduction) belong to a separate opt-in 'background adjustment' choice available to any background, not to these four ids.

problem: The Intimidation entry's `when` drops the form gate. The record reads "- **Humanoid Form** Animals can sense the power of your presence. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Intimidation checks against animals and beasts..." — the bonus exists only in Humanoid Form, but the spec's `when` is just 'to Intimidate animals and beasts (and no penalty for lacking a shared language)'. The same spec correctly writes 'in Yaoguai Form' on its second entry, and born-of-celestial and born-of-item both correctly carry 'Humanoid Form', so this is an internal inconsistency, not a deliberate reading.
correction: when: 'while in Humanoid Form, to Intimidate animals and beasts (and you take no penalty for lacking a shared language)'.

problem: Same dropped form gate. The record reads "- **Humanoid Form** You remain attuned to the natural world. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Survival checks to Sense Direction, and you don't take a penalty if you don't have a compass." The spec's `when` ('to Sense Direction (and you ignore the no-compass penalty)') omits Humanoid Form, so a player reading the star would think it applies in yaoguai form too.
correction: when: 'while in Humanoid Form, to Sense Direction (and you ignore the no-compass penalty)'.

problem: Same dropped form gate. The record reads "- **Humanoid Form** With fresh vegetation, you can better aid those in need. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Medicine checks to Administer First Aid." The spec's `when` is bare 'to Administer First Aid'. (The rest of this spec is right — the Yaoguai Form clause genuinely buffs someone else's Medicine check to Treat your Wounds and correctly has no entry.)
correction: when: 'while in Humanoid Form, to Administer First Aid'.

problem: Mis-targeted. The record says "a +2 status bonus to your Fortitude DC and Reflex DC against any effect that would move you or knock you prone" — that is the DC an opponent rolls against (Athletics to Shove/Trip/Grapple), which in PF2e is 10 + your save modifier, NOT your save roll. The spec still emits two entries with targetKind 'save' (fortitude and reflex), so the registry would put a star on the Fortitude and Reflex rows. A player opening those rows reads "+2 status" as a boost to the d20 roll — exactly the 'misleads the player' failure mode. The parenthetical disclaimer is buried inside the `bonus` string, which is rendered as the modifier text, not as a caveat.
correction: Emit NO bonus entries for this record. Keep situational: true only in the sense of 'has a conditional effect', set bonuses: [] with needsEngineWork: true / needsHumanDecision: true and the note that the target is a save DC (Fortitude DC / Reflex DC) for which the sheet has no stat — the target-kind list has 'ac' and 'classDc' but no save DC. If the owner later answers 'surface it on the save row', it must be re-added with the disclaimer in a dedicated field the sheet actually renders (e.g. folded into `when`: "this raises your Fortitude DC that an opponent rolls against — it does NOT add to your Fortitude save roll"), never in `bonus`. Everything else in the spec is confirmed: +2 status, 1-action Stand Firm, Frequency once per minute, effects last 1 round, 10 temporary HP is a play resource, and the ally-in-aura gap is real.

problem: Same defect as the Greater banner. Record text confirmed: "You and allies within your banner's aura gain 15 temporary Hit Points and a +3 status bonus to your Fortitude DC and Reflex DC against any effect that would move you or knock you prone. These effects last for 1 round." The +3 is a bonus to the DC opponents roll against, but the spec anchors it to targetKind 'save' (fortitude and reflex), which would display it as a bonus to the player's save rolls.
correction: Same correction: drop the two save entries, leave needsEngineWork: true (no save-DC stat) and needsHumanDecision: true. The numbers themselves are right (+3 status, 15 temp HP, 1-action Stand Firm, once per minute, 1 round).

problem: Condition invented / unconditional bonus marked situational, and internally inconsistent with the same author's own bomb rulings. The Crimson lens entry "+2 item (+4 on jaws Strikes) ... on melee Strike damage, while the Crimson Fulcrum Lens is invested" is starred as situational, but the record states no condition: "While you have the Crimson Fulcrum Lens invested ... You gain a +2 item bonus to saving throws against fear effects and a +2 item bonus to your melee Strike damage (this increases to a +4 item bonus to damage if the melee Strike is a jaws attack)." Every melee Strike gets it; 'melee' and 'jaws' are weapon scopes, not situations — exactly the reasoning the same specs used to declare the tenderizer grenades' flat '+2 item bonus to attack rolls' UNCONDITIONAL and 'part of that weapon's attack maths'. Starring it means the player sees a conditional marker on a bonus that always applies to their melee damage.
correction: Drop the strikeDamage entry from the situational list for the Crimson lens: classify it as unconditional-while-invested (+2 item to melee Strike damage, +4 item on jaws Strikes) and route it to the melee strike-damage maths, with needsEngineWork true because derive.ts has no lane for an invested item granting an item bonus to melee damage (grep of derive.ts shows damage item bonuses come only from runes/ABP/Monster Parts). Keep the other seven entries as authored — the fear-save +2 item (Crimson), the four Ebon +1 item entries, the Emerald +2 item vs magic for 1 round, and the Ochre +2 status vs emotion are all genuinely condition- or duration-gated and were verified word-for-word against the record.

problem: needsEngineWork is set to false, which is wrong and directly contradicts the same batch's ruling on aon-inubrix-armor. The bonus itself is right ("While wearing noqual armor, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC against spell attack rolls"), but this record is a precious-MATERIAL template, not a wearable suit: acBonus 0, no category, no group, price {}. A real character wears 'noqual half plate' — a base armor with the material applied — so an item lane that fires on 'the character has aon-noqual-armor equipped' will never trigger for a legitimate build, and if someone does equip the template it contributes 0 AC. The identical record aon-inubrix-armor was correctly flagged 'This is a precious-material template record (acBonus 0), not a wearable suit.'
correction: Keep the bonus ({+1 circumstance, to AC against spell attack rolls, while wearing this armor, targetKind ac}) but set needsEngineWork true with the note: material-template record — the marker must key off the base armor having the noqual material applied, which the item lane cannot currently express (same material lane already demanded for aon-inubrix-armor / aon-inubrix-weapon).

problem: Same defect as aon-noqual-armor: needsEngineWork false. The +1 circumstance to AC against spell attack rolls is correctly read from the text, but the record is a material template — acBonus 0, no category, no group, price {} (level 13) — describing what happens to armor 'crafted from' sovereign steel, not a suit a character can wear. The marker as specified can never fire on a real build, and the batch's own aon-inubrix-armor entry applies exactly this reasoning.
correction: Keep the bonus entry unchanged and set needsEngineWork true: 'precious-material template record — needs a material lane that applies sovereign steel to a base armor; the item lane cannot key a marker off a template the character never actually equips.'

problem: The condition is broadened beyond the record. The spec's 'when' reads 'on Recall Knowledge checks on subjects covered by the book (necromancy, Thassilonian rune magic, Runelord Zutha), while holding it'. The record says only: 'If the Kardosian Fragments are referenced as part of any attempt to Recall Knowledge on subjects associated with its contents, it grants a +3 item bonus to the skill check.' None of the three parenthetical subjects appears in that sentence, and 'while holding it' is a requirement of the separate Embrace the Void activation ('you're holding the Kardosian Fragments'), not of the Recall Knowledge bonus, which only requires the book to be 'referenced as part of' the attempt. Player-facing text that names subjects the book never claims to cover invites arguments at the table.
correction: Reword the condition to the record's own wording: when = 'when you reference the book as part of a Recall Knowledge attempt on a subject associated with its contents'. Bonus (+3 item), targetKind skill, skill 'all', situational true, and the temp-HP note are all correct as authored and should be kept.

problem: The target is a guess the record does not support, and it contradicts how the same batch handled every other Recall Knowledge bonus. The record says the holder 'must be trained in Survival' to USE the astrolabe (for latitude/date/time), then separately: 'An astrolabe also grants a +1 item bonus on checks to identify celestial bodies.' Identifying a celestial body is a Recall Knowledge check, which uses whichever knowledge skill or Lore fits — the very reason the-kardosian-fragments and aon-fixer were both keyed skill:'all'. Pinning it to Survival would star the wrong stat for a character who identifies the body with Nature or Astronomy Lore, and would star Survival for a use the text never grants.
correction: Change targetKind skill / skill 'survival' to skill 'all', keeping bonus '+1 item' and when = 'on checks to identify celestial bodies (a standard astrolabe only functions on steady ground; you must be trained in Survival to use it)'. Keep needsHumanDecision true with the same question, but restate it as 'confirm whether the +1 should be narrowed to Nature / a lore:astronomy key' rather than defaulting to Survival.

problem: The spec emits a populated bonuses[] entry (+1 circumstance, save:'all') while its own engineNote states that registering it would be a false positive on the athamaru's own saves. Anything downstream that ingests `bonuses` will star this character's Fort/Ref/Will for a bonus they provably never receive: the text reads "a 10-foot aura that grants any ALLY in it a +1 circumstance bonus to saving throws against fear" — allies only, never self.
correction: Set bonuses to an empty array (keep situational true only if the pipeline needs the record retained for the human decision, otherwise situational:false). The record grants zero modifiers to this character's own numbers; the ally aura must not be expressible as a registry entry until an ally-facing surface exists. Keep needsEngineWork/needsHumanDecision as authored — the question itself is the right one.

problem: The condition text is narrowed beyond the record. Core.json reads: "You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude or Reflex DC against attempts to Reposition, Shove, or Trip you. This bonus also applies to saving throws against spells or effects that attempt to move you or knock you prone." The second sentence names no defence, but the spec folds it into the Fortitude-only and Reflex-only entries, so a Will save against, e.g., a mental effect that knocks the leshy prone would show no marker.
correction: Keep the two DC entries but restrict their `when` text to the Reposition/Shove/Trip DC clause, and add a third entry: bonus '+2 circumstance', save 'all', when 'against spells or effects that try to move you or knock you prone'. That matches how the registry already keys unqualified "saving throws against X" wording (grave-orc, sewer-rat, chrysanthemum-leshy all use save:'all').

problem: needsEngineWork is set false, but the entry uses targetKind 'speed', which does not exist in the shipped registry. SituationalTarget in src/rules/situationalBonuses.ts declares kind: 'skill' | 'save' | 'perception' | 'ac' | 'attack', and all 419 existing target objects in that file use only those five (skill 199, save 141, perception 42, ac 35, attack 2). The entry cannot be written to the registry as specified.
correction: Set needsEngineWork true with the note: 'the +10-foot circumstance bonus to all Speeds while fleeing needs a `speed` target kind added to SituationalTarget (and a Speed row on the sheet that can carry a star); no existing kind fits.' The classification itself is right — it is conditional on holding the fleeing condition, so it must NOT be folded into the printed Speed.

problem: The engineNote misstates the record: "the record carries `loreChoices`-style freedom but no effectChoices block naming the Lore, so the chosen value may not even be recorded." The record carries no `loreChoices` field at all, and its only effectChoices block is `poppet-material` (fire/electricity/cold weakness). Contrast half-moon-sarangay in the same chunk, which really does carry `loreChoices: 2`.
correction: Reword to the verified fact: 'the record has no loreChoices field and no effectChoices naming the Lore (its only effectChoices block is poppet-material), so the player\'s chosen Lore is definitively not stored anywhere — the star has nothing to attach to until the heritage records its Lore grant.' The +2/+3 Helpful Poppet observation and the human-decision question are both correct and should stay.

problem: The engineNote describes the second rider as lowering "the flat check to notice a concealed target to DC 3 / a hidden one to DC 9". The record says the opposite direction of use: "When you TARGET an opponent that is concealed from you or hidden from you, reduce the DC of the flat check to 3 for a concealed target or 9 for a hidden one." It is the flat check to successfully affect a concealed/hidden target (normally DC 5 / DC 11), not a check to notice one.
correction: Reword the note to 'when you target a concealed opponent the flat check drops from DC 5 to DC 3, and from DC 11 to DC 9 for a hidden one'. The registry entry itself (+2 circumstance, perception, Seek within 30 feet, only if you can hear and the creature can make sound) is correct and needs no change.

problem: The engineNote claims Track is 'a Survival activity (verified against core.json\'s actions entry)'. That verification did not happen: core.json's actions.track record has no `skill` field, and its description has the skill reference stripped (it reads "using the rules" where the Survival link was). Nothing in core.json states the skill.
correction: The conclusion is right — Track is a Survival exploration activity in PF2e, so the star belongs on Survival — but the note must not cite core.json as the source. Say 'Track is a Survival activity per the PF2e rules; core.json\'s actions.track carries no skill field, so the mapping is rules knowledge, not data.' Worth flagging separately that actions.track has a stripped skill reference.

problem: The classification (situational:false) is right, but the engineNote is factually wrong about the app: it says the +1 "needs a stored choice plus an attuned flag before it can enter the maths", implying the choice mechanism does not exist. It already does. core.json has an `effectChoices` field used by 29 items, and it is wired end-to-end (src/rules/types.ts documents it, src/rules/build.ts resolves it into `chosenEffects` / `resolvedItemPassives` for worn items, src/builder/Builder.tsx + shared.tsx render the picker). `druids-crown` and `eidolon-cape` are exactly this pattern — pick one of N, each option granting `passive.skills.<skill> = N`.
correction: Keep situational:false. Rewrite the note to: orc-warmask simply has no authored `effectChoices` block; it needs one choice with the four sources mapping to passive.skills religion / nature / arcana / occultism = 1 (The Gods / The Land / Magic / The Unknown). Only the 50 gp attunement GATE is unmodelled — express it inside the same block (either a 5th "chosen but not attuned" option, or 8 options = 4 skills x attuned/not), since a bare 4-option block would hand the +1 to a character who never paid for the ceremony. Narrow the human-decision question to just the attunement representation; do not ask whether a per-item choice lane should be built.

problem: The engineNote names only one missing unconditional piece — "the armor's built-in *+2 greater resilient* runes, whose +2 item bonus to ALL saves is unconditional and is NOT represented anywhere in the record's fields". It misses that the potency half of the same rune string is missing too: the record's acBonus is 6, dexCap 0, checkPenalty -3, speedPenalty -10, strength 4, which is byte-for-byte the BASE full-plate record (d.items['full-plate'] = acBonus 6, dexCap 0, cp -3, sp -10, str 4). So the "+2" potency rune's +2 item bonus to AC is absent as well.
correction: Note BOTH gaps: the +2 potency (item bonus to AC) and the greater resilient (+2 item bonus to saves) are unrepresented. Also widen the scope note — this is systemic, not per-item: 93 armor records name built-in runes in their prose and none carry them in any field (there is no runes/potency/resilient field in the item schema at all). Classification of the +2 status vs fear as situational is correct and unaffected.

problem: Same omission as hero's plate. The note says only "the base *+2 greater resilient* runes' unconditional +2 item bonus to saves is also absent from the record's fields". The record is acBonus 6 / dexCap 0 / checkPenalty -3 / speedPenalty -10 / strength 4 — identical to base full-plate — so the +2 potency item bonus to AC is missing too, and passiveEffects contains only grantsLanguages: ['thalassic'].
correction: State that both the +2 AC potency and the +2 save resilient are missing from the fields. The +2 item bonus to Athletics to Swim as the only situational entry is correct.

problem: needsHumanDecision is set to false even though the spec's own engineNote says entry 2 ("to your Deception DC against a creature using Sense Motive on you") is "a DC-side bonus rather than a check bonus — same display gap as Olfactory Obfuscator". The identical situation on olfactory-obfuscator-lesser was flagged needsHumanDecision:true with a question about whether DC-only bonuses get a star. The same unanswered question decides whether this entry may be written at all, so the flag contradicts the note.
correction: Set needsHumanDecision:true with the same question ("Should DC-only bonuses be shown as a star on the related skill with DC-only wording, or suppressed until the sheet can display skill DCs?"), so the owner's single ruling is recorded against every record it governs. The two check-side entries (+1 circumstance Deception to Lie, +1 circumstance Intimidation to Coerce) are correct and can ship regardless of the ruling.

problem: The engineNote's supporting citation is misleading: "core.json carries no field for an alchemical bomb's item bonus to attack (compare alchemists-fire-lesser, which has none to carry)". alchemists-fire-lesser's text grants no attack bonus at ALL ("deals 1d8 fire damage, 1 persistent fire damage, and 1 fire splash damage" — full stop), so it demonstrates nothing about whether the schema could carry one.
correction: The underlying claim is right — I enumerated every field name across d.items and there is no attackBonus/itemBonus field anywhere (fields are: acBonus, activationCost, apexAttribute, baseItem, brokenThreshold, bulk, capacity, category, checkPenalty, consumableType, counters, damage, descRefs, description, dexCap, dynamicSkillBonus, edition, effectChoices, frequency, grantedStrikes, grantsFeats, group, hands, hardness, heldSpells, hp, id, ignoredBulk, innateSpells, itemType, level, material, maxHpBonus, name, negativeHealing, passiveEffects, price, range, rarity, reload, source, speedPenalty, spellSlot, strength, strikeDamage, traits, usage, uses, value). Swap the citation to alchemists-fire-moderate/greater, which DO print "+1/+2 item bonus to attack rolls" in prose and still carry no field — that is the actual proof, and it shows the gap spans the whole bomb catalogue, not just these 10 records.

problem: The spec is faithful to the record, but its engineNote ("Identical bonus to the Greater version; this one simply lacks the temporary Hit Points" / the greater's +3) launders what looks like a data defect instead of flagging it. The level-18 Greater record's own text reads "For 1 hour after consuming a bowl of improved Lastwall soup, you gain a +3 item bonus" — it names the IMPROVED soup, and grants the same +3 as the level-10 lastwall-soup-improved, while the level-1 base lastwall-soup grants +2. A three-grade line reading +2 / +3 / +3 with the top grade quoting the middle grade's name is almost certainly a copy-paste in core.json.
correction: Keep the +3 (the record's own text is the authority for this pass) and keep the entry situational with skill/stealth, but add needsHumanDecision:true or a data flag: "lastwall-soup-greater's description names the *improved* soup and repeats its +3; re-check the printed value against AoN before the registry hard-codes +3 for both grades." Everything else in both soup specs (item type, 1-hour window, temp HP correctly excluded from an 'hp' entry) is correct.

problem: Marked situational:true while emitting ZERO bonuses. The record's own text — "When you affix these ... to the hooves of an ordinary horse or a quadrupedal animal companion and the animal companion invests them, that creature gains a +5-foot item bonus to its land Speed and a +2 circumstance bonus to Athletics checks" — gives everything to the mount, nothing to the PC. That is the same situation as aon-tyrant-s-writ (bonus to the summoned undead) and aon-fan-of-the-four-winds (bonus to the vessel), which this same engineer correctly marked situational:false. A true flag with an empty bonuses array is internally inconsistent and will read downstream as "this record has situational bonuses" when it stars nothing.
correction: Set situational:false with reasonIfNot: "Both typed bonuses are granted to the horse or quadrupedal animal companion that invests the horseshoes ('that creature gains...'), never to the wearer's own stats, so nothing on the character sheet should be starred." Keep needsEngineWork:true and the existing engineNote about the missing companion-stat target kind, and keep the passiveEffects.speedBonus 5 warning — I confirmed it is a live bug (derive.ts:1584 adds it to the PC's land Speed).

problem: Condition narrowed beyond the record's own text. The spec's when reads "on Athletics checks to Swim, while wearing the helmet with the visor down", but the visor-down clause belongs to the PRECEDING sentence ("While wearing the helmet with the visor down, you can see, hear, and speak clearly underwater."); the Swim bonus is its own sentence — "You also have a +1 item bonus to Athletics checks to Swim." Foundry's submersible-helmet.json backs this up: the FlatModifier is predicated only on ["action:swim"], with no visor gate. Minor, but it is an added condition a player could be told they fail to meet.
correction: when: "on Athletics checks to Swim (+2 with the greater helm)" — drop "with the visor down". Everything else in this spec (item type, athletics target, +1/+2 scaling) is correct.

problem: The engineNote states a contested rules reading as settled fact: "The saves half only does anything if the armor also has a resilient rune (that's the item bonus being increased)." The record only says "the item bonus it provides to AC and saving throws increases by 1 against spells" — it does not say a resilient rune is a prerequisite, and the opposite reading (0 + 1 = a +1 item bonus to saves vs spells even with no resilient rune) is equally available. Acting on the note would hide a bonus a player may be entitled to. The two emitted bonus entries themselves are correct under either reading.
correction: Keep both bonus entries as authored, but soften the note to an ambiguity and raise it rather than resolve it: set needsHumanDecision:true with the question "Does keep stone armor's +1 to saves vs spells require an existing item bonus to saves (a resilient rune) to increase, or does it stand alone? The text only says the item bonus 'increases by 1'." Do not gate the display on the armor having a resilient rune.
